question: A technician is writing a firewall rule so that staff email clients can download mail from the provider's server with POP3. Which destination port must the rule allow?
explanation: POP3 clients collect mail from the server on TCP port 110. Port 143 is IMAP, which also collects mail but leaves it on the server, port 25 is SMTP for relaying mail between servers, and port 587 is where mail clients sign in to send outgoing mail.

question: A desktop monitor's picture has become so dark that it can be seen only with a flashlight held close to the screen, and raising the brightness in the monitor's menu changes nothing. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A damaged or loose video cable
explanation: A faint picture that appears under a flashlight shows that the panel is still forming the image and only its light source has failed, which points to the backlight. A failing graphics card produces artifacts or no picture at all, a damaged or loose cable causes flicker, lines or signal loss, and a wrong input brings a no-signal message rather than a dim image.

question: An office PC with 4 GB of RAM becomes very slow whenever several browser tabs and a spreadsheet are open, and its drive activity light then stays lit. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: File system errors on the drive
A drive controller set to IDE mode
explanation: When open programs need more memory than is installed, Windows keeps moving pages of memory out to the page file on the drive, and that constant paging holds the activity light on and makes the PC crawl until more RAM is added. File system errors cause read failures at any load, a failing memory module causes crashes and stop errors rather than slowness, and a controller left in IDE mode makes the drive slower all the time, not only when many programs are open.

question: A database server handles a constant stream of small random reads and needs the lowest possible read latency. Which storage should it use?
options: SATA SSD on a 6 Gb/s port
NVMe SSD on a PCIe 4.0 x4 link
explanation: An NVMe SSD reaches the processor over PCIe lanes with no moving parts and very little protocol overhead, so it gives the lowest random read latency. A SATA SSD also has no moving parts but is held back by the older AHCI command set and its 6 Gb/s link, a 15,000 RPM SAS drive still waits for the platter to turn, and a RAID 5 set of 7,200 RPM drives spreads reads across disks but keeps each disk's mechanical delay.

question: A user sends a confidential report to a shared office printer and does not want it to print until they enter a code at the device. Which feature provides this?
explanation: Secure print release holds a job at the printer until the user enters a PIN or taps a badge, so that confidential pages do not sit in the output tray. Audit logging records who printed what, print spooling queues jobs and sends them on as soon as the printer is free, and a cloud printing service lets users print from anywhere.

question: A technician is placing the only wireless access point that will serve a single-story office. Which location gives the BEST coverage?
options: In a corner of the office, on a desk
At the center of the office, on a desk
At the center of the office, on the ceiling
In a corner of the office, mounted on the ceiling
explanation: An access point with omnidirectional antennas spreads its signal in every direction, so mounting it high and near the middle of the space gives the most even coverage with the fewest obstructions. From a corner, much of the coverage falls outside the building, and at desk height, furniture, equipment and people absorb the signal before it reaches the far side of the office.

question: A user wants one cable that can charge a laptop, carry video to a monitor and be plugged in either way up at both ends. Which connector does this cable use?
explanation: USB-C is a reversible 24-pin connector that is the same at both ends of the cable and can carry data, video and enough power to charge a laptop. USB-A fits only one way up and is found on the host end. Micro-USB is a small one-way connector for older phones and accessories. Lightning is reversible, but it is Apple's connector for phones and tablets and does not charge laptops or sit at both ends of a cable.

question: Which kind of laptop storage plugs into a keyed edge connector and is sold in sizes such as 2242, 2260 and 2280?
explanation: M.2 cards plug into a keyed edge connector and are named by their width and length in millimeters, so a 2280 card is 22 mm wide and 80 mm long. An mSATA card is 30 mm wide and uses an older mini PCIe-style connector with no size code, a 2.5-inch drive sits in a case with SATA data and power connectors, and eMMC storage is a chip soldered to the system board.

question: A technician connects a replacement hard drive to a desktop. At power-on the drive makes a loud, repeating click, and the firmware does not detect it. What does this MOST likely indicate?
explanation: A loud, repeating click from a hard drive that is not detected is the classic sign of failing read/write heads, often called the click of death, so the drive should not be used. Heads make only a soft sound as they load at spin-up, a loose SATA data cable stops detection without any clicking, and a SMART self-test runs quietly on a drive that is still detected.

question: A reviewer notes that a laptop uses an IPS panel rather than a TN or VA panel. Compared with those two LCD types, what is an IPS panel known for?
options: Fast pixel response at a low price
High contrast with deep black levels
explanation: An IPS (in-plane switching) panel keeps its color accurate across wide viewing angles, which makes it the usual LCD choice for photo and design work. Fast response at a low price describes TN, which has the narrowest viewing angles. High contrast with deep blacks describes VA. Pixels that light themselves belong to OLED, which is not an LCD technology and needs no backlight.

question: A user prints a portrait report on both sides of the paper. When the sheets are turned like the pages of a book, the fronts read normally but every back page is upside down. Which setting is the most likely cause?
options: Flip on the short edge is selected
explanation: For a portrait document printed on both sides, flipping on the long edge keeps each back page upright when the sheets are turned like a book, while flipping on the short edge turns every back page upside down. Landscape orientation would change the layout of every page, reverse page order changes only the sequence of the pages, and booklet printing places two reduced pages side by side on each face of every sheet.

question: A three-year-old phone now needs charging twice a day, although the way it is used has not changed. Its battery settings show a maximum capacity of 71 percent. What will restore its original battery life?
explanation: Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity as they age, and a maximum capacity of about 70 percent shows a worn battery, so only a new battery brings back the original runtime. Calibrating corrects an inaccurate charge reading, a higher-wattage charger only shortens charging time, and a factory reset helps when software is draining the battery, not when the battery itself holds less charge.

question: Colors on a user's monitor look oversaturated on one Windows PC, with reds too deep and blues leaning toward purple. The same monitor, cable and input look correct on another PC. Which setting on the first PC MOST likely causes this?
options: The refresh rate for the display
The color profile for the display
The color depth for the display
The Night light strength in Windows
explanation: A color profile tells Windows how to map colors for a particular display, so the wrong profile can shift hues and oversaturate colors on that PC alone. Night light adds a warm amber tint, too low a color depth shows banding in gradients, and an unsupported refresh rate brings an out-of-range message or a blank screen rather than shifted colors.

question: An ISP can no longer obtain new blocks of public IPv4 space for its customers. Which property of IPv6 solves this shortage?
explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long against 32 bits in IPv4, so the number of possible addresses rises from about 4.3 billion to 2 to the power of 128, which ends the shortage. A fixed 40-byte header makes packets simpler for routers to process, stateless autoconfiguration lets hosts set up their own addresses without DHCP, and colon-hexadecimal notation is only the way an address is written, so none of them adds addresses.

question: A growing firm's database server has slowed down. Its two mirrored hard drives are completing as many small random reads and writes per second as they are rated for, with long queues, and S.M.A.R.T. and the RAID utility report no errors. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A failing drive in the mirrored pair
A degraded array that is rebuilding
explanation: When drives already complete as many input/output operations per second (IOPS) as they are rated for and requests still queue up, the workload has outgrown them, and faster storage such as SSDs is the fix. A failing drive or a faulty SATA cable would show up as errors in S.M.A.R.T., and a degraded or rebuilding mirror would be reported by the RAID utility.

question: A cable internet subscriber's downloads are fast in the morning but slow every evening, even though the modem and the home network test normally. Which characteristic of cable service explains this?
options: Trees can block line of sight to a tower
Each signal makes a round trip to orbit
Homes on one node share the same bandwidth
Speed drops with distance from the exchange
explanation: Cable internet runs DOCSIS over a coaxial network in which every home on a node shares the same channel capacity, so speeds fall when many neighbors are online in the evening. Loss of speed with distance from the exchange is a DSL trait, a round trip to a satellite adds delay to satellite service, and line of sight to a tower matters for a wireless ISP, and none of these changes with the time of day.

question: After a user returns from a distant meeting room, their laptop stays connected to the access point there, 150 feet away, and drops often, although an access point with the same SSID is 20 feet away. Turning Wi-Fi off and on fixes it. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The near access point has reached its client limit
The laptop does not roam to the closer access point
The near access point blocks the laptop's MAC
The two access points use the same radio channel
explanation: A sticky client is a device that keeps its association with a distant access point instead of roaming to a stronger one nearby, so it suffers a weak signal and drops until it reconnects. Joining the near access point after a Wi-Fi restart shows that it has room for the laptop and does not block its MAC address, and a shared channel would slow every client rather than tie one laptop to a far access point.

question: A technician turns on a smartphone's hotspot. A laptop, the only device trying to join, lists the hotspot's network name but fails to connect to it. What is the likely cause?
options: Bluetooth is turned off on the laptop
The laptop has the wrong password
The phone is hiding its network name
Mobile data is turned off on the phone
explanation: When a device can see a hotspot's network name but cannot join it, the usual cause is a wrong Wi-Fi password, because the hotspot is broadcasting and only the authentication is failing. Mobile data turned off would leave the hotspot with no internet connection to share rather than make it reject the laptop, and a hidden network name would keep the hotspot out of the laptop's list. Bluetooth is needed for Bluetooth tethering, not for a Wi-Fi hotspot.

question: A laptop's specification sheet lists 802.11ax as its newest wireless standard. Which generation name does the Wi-Fi Alliance use for that standard?
explanation: The Wi-Fi Alliance markets 802.11ax as Wi-Fi 6, and 802.11ax devices that can also use the 6 GHz band are sold as Wi-Fi 6E. Wi-Fi 4 is the name given to 802.11n, Wi-Fi 5 the name given to 802.11ac, and Wi-Fi 7 the name given to the newer 802.11be standard.

question: A user's laptop has a 256 GB SSD, but her synced cloud folder holds 1 TB. She wants everything in it listed in File Explorer, using local space only for the items she opens. Which sync client feature should she use?
explanation: Files on demand keeps every file visible in the synced folder but downloads its contents only when it is opened, so a large library fits on a small drive. Selective folder sync leaves unchosen folders off the device entirely, pausing stops syncing for a time, and version history keeps earlier copies of each file. OneDrive calls the feature Files On-Demand, and other services call such files online-only.

question: Small dark marks repeat down every page from a laser printer, always the same distance apart. Which check identifies the component that is leaving them?
options: Match the gap to each rotating part's circumference
Print the same file from a different computer
Inspect the pickup roller's rubber for glazing and wear
Read the toner level on a supplies status page
explanation: Marks that repeat at a fixed spacing come from a rotating part, and the spacing equals the circumference of the drum or roller that leaves them, so matching the two identifies the part. The toner level explains faded pages, printing from another computer separates a computer fault from a printer fault, and a glazed or worn pickup roller causes misfeeds rather than marks.

question: Which feature of DDR5 memory modules is new compared with DDR4 modules?
options: A power management IC on the module
More pins on the edge connector
A higher operating voltage than DDR4
explanation: DDR5 modules carry their own power management IC (PMIC), which regulates voltage on the module instead of relying on the motherboard as DDR4 does. DDR5 actually runs at a lower 1.1 volts than DDR4's 1.2 volts, both use 288-pin DIMMs with the notch in different places, and DDR5 splits each module into two 32-bit subchannels rather than one 64-bit channel.

question: A four-year-old laptop that sits on a desk runs hot, and its fan stays at full speed even at idle. Cleaning the dust out of the vents and fan made no difference. What should the technician do NEXT?
options: Replace the thermal paste on the CPU
Use the laptop on a hard flat surface
Change the power plan to balanced
explanation: Thermal paste fills the tiny gaps between the processor and its heat sink, and once it dries out after a few years, heat stays in the chip, so temperatures and fan speed stay high even at light load. A fan that runs at full speed is working, the power plan changes clock speeds rather than how well heat leaves the chip, and a hard flat surface helps only when soft material is blocking the vents.

question: In which cloud service model does the customer manage just its users and data, while the provider runs everything from the hardware up to the application itself?
explanation: In software as a service the provider runs the hardware, operating system, platform and application, leaving the customer to manage its users and data. Platform as a service leaves the customer its own application code, infrastructure as a service leaves it the operating system and everything above, and desktop as a service leaves it the programs and settings inside each hosted desktop.

question: In a structured cabling installation, what role does the patch panel in the wiring closet play?
options: It supplies power to phones over the cable
It terminates the cable runs from wall jacks
It regenerates signals over long cable runs
It forwards each frame to its destination port
explanation: A patch panel is the fixed end point for the horizontal runs from wall jacks, so short patch cables can connect any jack to any switch port without disturbing the permanent cabling. It is a passive device, while a switch forwards frames to the right port, a repeater regenerates signals on long runs, and a PoE switch or injector supplies power over the cable.

question: A laptop shows vertical colored lines on its built-in screen, and the same lines appear on an external monitor and on the firmware startup screen. Which component is MOST likely at fault?
explanation: Lines that appear on the built-in screen, on an external monitor and even before Windows loads come from the hardware the outputs share, the graphics processor or its memory. A damaged LCD panel or ribbon cable affects only the built-in screen, and a driver fault cannot reach the firmware startup screen, which is drawn before any driver loads.

question: A privacy filter is fitted to the display of a laptop used in a shared office. What does the filter do?
options: It shields the panel from scratches and cracks.
It darkens the screen for anyone viewing from the side.
It filters out blue light from the display.
It cuts reflections from lamps and windows.
explanation: A privacy filter uses tiny louvers that darken the screen for anyone outside a narrow viewing angle, which stops shoulder surfing by people beside the user. Cutting reflections is the job of an anti-glare filter, removing blue light is the job of a blue-light filter, and resisting scratches and cracks is the job of a tempered glass protector.

question: A user must install an older operating system that boots only in legacy BIOS mode, but the motherboard firmware is UEFI. Which firmware option must be enabled to allow this?
explanation: The Compatibility Support Module (CSM) lets UEFI firmware present a legacy BIOS interface so that older operating systems and boot loaders can start, and Secure Boot normally has to be off while it is used. TPM is a chip that stores keys and measures the boot process, VT-x lets an Intel processor run virtual machines, and PXE starts a computer from an image on the network.

question: A network printer received a new IP address last week. Users who print through the print server are unaffected, but one PC that connects to the printer directly by its address now shows it offline. What should the technician do?
options: Reinstall the printer driver on that PC
Update the printer port on that PC
Restart the Print Spooler service on that PC
Clear the stalled jobs from that PC's queue
explanation: A Standard TCP/IP port stores the printer's IP address, so a PC that prints through one loses the printer when the address changes, until the port is updated to the new address. Reinstalling the driver fixes garbled output, restarting the Print Spooler revives a hung spooler, and clearing stalled jobs unblocks a queue, but none of them changes the address the PC sends its jobs to.

question: A company installs access points on all three floors of its headquarters so that employees' laptops and tablets connect to the office network over Wi-Fi. Which network type does this create?
explanation: A wireless LAN connects devices by Wi-Fi within one site, such as a building or a campus, and joins them to the same local network as the wired hosts. A wireless PAN such as Bluetooth reaches only a few meters around one person, a wireless MAN covers a city, and a wireless WAN such as a cellular data network spans regions or countries.

question: A technician must move a VM's operating system, installed programs and user files to a new host. Which of the VM's files holds all of them?
explanation: A VM's virtual disk file, such as a VHDX file in Hyper-V or a VMDK file in VMware, holds everything the guest stores on its drive, including the operating system, programs and user files. The configuration file holds only settings such as memory size and processor count, the installation ISO file is the media the guest was installed from, and a saved memory state file holds the contents of RAM while the VM is suspended.

question: A smartphone's status bar shows LTE next to the signal bars. Which generation of cellular technology is the phone connected to?
explanation: LTE (Long Term Evolution) is the 4G cellular standard, so a phone that shows LTE is connected to a 4G network. 3G networks used technologies such as UMTS and HSPA, 2G networks used GSM and EDGE, and a 5G connection uses New Radio (NR) and appears as 5G in the status bar.

question: A user's phone shows full LTE signal bars, and websites and app downloads still load, but far more slowly than usual. What is the likely cause?
options: The plan's high-speed data is used up
explanation: Many mobile plans slow a line's data once its monthly high-speed allowance is used up, so the phone keeps full signal bars while every download crawls. Incorrect APN settings, or data roaming turned off while abroad, would stop mobile data entirely rather than slow it, and airplane mode would remove the signal bars altogether.

question: A technician must find which of 48 unlabeled cables at the back of a patch panel runs to one office's wall jack, without disconnecting any of them. Which tool should be used?
explanation: A toner probe kit traces cables: the tone generator is connected to the cable at the wall jack, and the inductive probe is passed along the cables at the patch panel until it picks up the tone, without disconnecting anything at the panel. A cable tester checks wiring once both ends are known and connected to it, a punchdown tool terminates wires on the panel, and a loopback plug tests a port.

question: Users cannot open the company intranet by name. Pinging the server by name returns an unknown host error, but pinging its IP address works. Which server role is most likely failing?
explanation: A DNS server translates hostnames into IP addresses, so a ping that fails by name but works by address points to a name resolution problem. A failed web server would make the site fail by address as well, and AAA and NTP servers handle sign-in and clock synchronization rather than name lookups.

question: A branch office sends its internet traffic through the main office. Since its router was replaced, branch users reach main office servers by name and by IP address but cannot reach any internet address. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The branch DNS server has stopped answering
The new router lacks a default route
The router's WAN link has gone down
The branch DHCP scope has run out
explanation: A router sends traffic for networks it has no specific route to along its default route (0.0.0.0/0), so a replacement router set up with only the company's internal routes reaches the main office but has no path to the internet. Names that resolve show that DNS works, main office servers that answer show that the WAN link is up, and users who can reach them clearly have addresses from DHCP.

question: Office PCs map a drive letter to shared department folders over SMB. Which server role provides those folders?
explanation: A file server shares folders over SMB on port 445, and users usually reach them as mapped drive letters with access controlled by permissions. A mail server stores and relays email, a web server delivers pages over HTTP or HTTPS, and an AAA server checks who users are and what they may do but does not hold the folders.

question: After a technician replaces a laptop's display assembly, the screen and webcam work, but Wi-Fi finds only a few networks and the signal is weak. What was most likely missed?
options: Reinstalling the driver for the Wi-Fi adapter
Reconnecting the antenna leads to the Wi-Fi card
Reseating the Wi-Fi card in its slot on the board
Turning the Wi-Fi radio back on in Windows settings
explanation: A laptop's Wi-Fi antennas sit in the display lid and connect to the Wi-Fi card by thin cables, so a new display assembly whose antenna leads are left unplugged gives a weak signal. A missing driver or a radio that is turned off would show no networks at all, and a card that is not seated would not be detected by Windows.

question: A technician is asked to plug an external drive into the fastest USB Type-A port on an older desktop. Some of the ports have blue plastic inserts and the rest are black. Which USB version do the blue ports normally indicate?
explanation: A blue insert in a USB Type-A port normally marks USB 3.0, the SuperSpeed version that carries up to 5 Gbps. USB 2.0 ports, limited to 480 Mbps, are usually black, and USB 1.1 ports, limited to 12 Mbps, were usually white. USB4 runs only over the USB-C connector, so a Type-A port cannot be USB4.

question: An office stops printing directly from each PC to the printers and sends every job through a dedicated print server instead. Which benefit does this give the office?
options: Managing shared queues in one place
explanation: A print server holds the queues for shared printers, so staff can view, pause, reorder or delete jobs and update drivers in one place instead of on every PC. Scanning straight to email is a feature of the copier itself, automatic toner reordering comes from a managed print service or the printer vendor, and Wi-Fi Direct lets a device connect straight to a printer without joining a network.

question: An office replaced its 100 Mbps switch with a Gigabit switch. Every workstation has a Gigabit network card, yet each link still connects at only 100 Mbps. What should the technician check?
options: The PoE power budget of the switch
The category of the network cabling
The speed of the office internet plan
The VLAN assigned to each switch port
explanation: Gigabit Ethernet over copper needs Category 5e cable or better, and CompTIA rates plain Category 5 for 100 Mbps, so links on older cabling settle at the lower speed whatever the switch supports. A VLAN decides which network a port joins, a PoE budget decides which devices the switch can power, and the internet plan limits traffic to the internet rather than the speed at which a workstation links to the switch.

question: A tablet shows a "Charging slowly" message each time it is plugged in. The message first appeared after the user began using the charger from an old phone. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: An app is draining the battery
The adapter's output is too low
explanation: A tablet needs far more power than an old phone charger can deliver, so a low-output adapter triggers the slow-charging warning and takes much longer to fill the battery. A damaged port gives a connection that drops out or works only at an angle, a battery that has lost capacity runs down sooner, and an app draining the battery shortens the time between charges.

question: A workstation's memory module is labeled DDR4-3200. What does the number 3200 measure?
options: Millions of clock cycles each second
Megabytes of data moved each second
explanation: The 3200 in DDR4-3200 is the data rate in megatransfers per second (MT/s): data moves on both edges of a 1600 MHz clock, giving 3200 million transfers each second. The clock itself runs at 1600 MHz, the bandwidth is about 25,600 MB/s (hence the PC4-25600 label), and CAS latency is a separate figure counted in clock cycles.

question: A technician setting up a new SOHO router changes its administrator password before touching any other setting. Which risk does this step remove?
options: The Wi-Fi passphrase can be guessed offline
The factory login is listed online
The firmware contains a known security flaw
The network name reveals the router brand
explanation: Default administrator credentials are printed in manuals and listed online for each router model, so anyone who reaches the login page of a router that still uses them can take full control of it. The Wi-Fi passphrase is a separate setting that resists offline guessing when it is long or protected by WPA3, a known firmware flaw is fixed by a firmware update, and a network name that reveals the brand is fixed by changing the SSID.

question: A technician must connect 16 wired computers, each to its own port, so that each frame leaves only through the port where its destination computer is attached. Which device should be installed?
explanation: A switch learns which MAC address is on each port and sends each frame only out of the port where its destination is attached. A hub repeats every frame out of all its ports, a repeater only regenerates the signal between two cable segments, and a bridge filters by MAC address but joins just two segments instead of giving each computer its own port.

question: A monitor connected to a laptop with a USB-C to DisplayPort cable shows no image, even with its DisplayPort input selected. The cable works with another laptop, and the monitor works with this laptop over HDMI. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Windows has switched the external display off
The USB-C port cannot send a video signal
The monitor is set to the wrong input
The cable is a USB 2.0 charging cable
explanation: A USB-C port carries video only if it supports DisplayPort Alternate Mode or Thunderbolt, and many laptops have USB-C ports that handle data and charging but no video. A USB 2.0 charging cable lacks the wires for video and would fail with every laptop, the DisplayPort input is already selected, and a setting that switched the external display off would also have blanked it over HDMI.

question: A workstation has a valid IP configuration and can ping its default gateway, but the user cannot reach any website or any server on other subnets. What should the technician do NEXT?
options: Replace the patch cable at the wall jack
Ping a remote address and then a name
Release and renew the workstation's lease
explanation: A reply from the gateway proves that the cable, adapter and local settings work, so the next test is a ping to a remote IP address, which checks routing, followed by a ping to a host name, which checks DNS. Renewing the lease, replacing the cable or reinstalling the driver would repeat work on parts that the gateway ping has already shown to be working.

question: A parent wants to stop the children's devices from reaching adult and gambling websites at home, without installing software on each device. Which router setting should be configured?
explanation: Content filtering on the router blocks websites by category for every device on the network, with nothing to install on each device. MAC filtering decides which devices may join the network at all, port forwarding opens a path for inbound connections from the internet, and a guest network keeps visitors away from home devices without limiting which sites they can visit.

question: A monitoring server must receive the SNMP alerts that switches send on their own, such as when a link goes down. On which UDP port should the server listen?
explanation: SNMP agents send traps, the alerts a device raises on its own, to the management station on UDP port 162. The station polls agents for readings on UDP port 161, while UDP ports 67 and 68 are the server and client ports of DHCP, which hands out IP addresses.

question: On one office floor, new devices sometimes get a correct 10.10.20.x address and sometimes a 192.168.0.x address with gateway 192.168.0.1, even on the same switch port. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The DHCP scope has run out of addresses
A rogue DHCP server is on the network
The switch port is on the guest VLAN
Two devices share one static address
explanation: Clients that receive a foreign address range and gateway only some of the time are getting answers from a second, unauthorized DHCP server, often a home router plugged in by an employee, which wins whenever it replies first. A full scope gives new clients no lease at all, a port on the guest VLAN would get the guest range every time, and a duplicate static address causes a conflict warning rather than a different range. DHCP snooping on managed switches blocks such offers.

question: After two years of daily use, an OLED laptop screen shows a faint outline of the taskbar that stays visible even while a full-screen video plays. What is this defect called?
explanation: Each OLED pixel makes its own light and wears with use, so an element shown in the same place for years, such as a taskbar, wears its pixels unevenly and leaves a permanent burn-in. Backlight bleed is light leaking at the edges of an LCD, which an OLED screen does not have, screen tearing splits moving images when frames and refresh fall out of step, and stuck pixels are single dots fixed on one color.

question: A smartphone gets hot and loses most of its charge within a few hours, even while it lies unused on a desk with the screen off. What is the MOST likely cause?
explanation: Heat and fast drain while a phone lies idle with the screen off mean something is keeping the processor busy, most often an app or malware running in the background, which the battery usage screen will name. A worn battery holds less charge but does not heat a phone at rest, brightness costs nothing while the screen is off, and Bluetooth draws very little power when idle.

question: The day after a PC's network adapter receives an update, Windows begins stopping at random with a blue screen that names the adapter's .sys file. What should the technician do FIRST?
explanation: When a stop error names a driver file and begins right after that driver was updated, the first fix is to roll the driver back to the version that worked, from Device Manager or in Safe Mode. System File Checker repairs damaged Windows files, a memory diagnostic tests RAM when stop codes point to memory, and reseating the adapter fixes a card that is loose or not detected.

question: A laptop screen flickers when the lid is opened to about 90 degrees, but the picture is steady at 45 and at 120 degrees. What is the MOST likely cause?
explanation: A fault that comes and goes with the angle of the lid is mechanical, and the part that flexes as the lid moves is the display cable running through the hinge. A failing graphics processor, an outdated driver or a wrong refresh rate would affect the screen at every angle, and a graphics fault would usually show on an external monitor as well.

question: A developer installs VirtualBox as an application on a Windows 11 laptop to run a Linux VM for testing. Which kind of virtualization software is VirtualBox?
explanation: VirtualBox is a Type 2, or hosted, hypervisor: it runs as an application on an existing operating system and relies on that host for access to the hardware. A Type 1 hypervisor such as VMware ESXi installs directly on the hardware, a container engine such as Docker runs isolated applications that share the host's kernel, and a system emulator such as QEMU imitates a complete computer, often one with a different processor.

question: The company requires a screen lock on every employee phone, but one user turned the lock off in the phone's settings. Which MDM feature should the administrator use to prevent this?
explanation: An MDM passcode policy requires a screen lock on enrolled devices and stops users from removing it, and the MDM can flag or block any device that falls out of compliance. Remote wipe erases a lost or stolen device, full-device encryption protects stored data, and an application deny list blocks named apps; none of them stops a user from switching off the lock.

question: A user wants one cable from a laptop to a desk dock that charges the laptop at 85 W, carries USB data and drives two 4K monitors. Which laptop port is designed for this?
explanation: Thunderbolt 4 runs over a USB-C connector and carries laptop charging by USB Power Delivery, 40 Gbps of data and video for two 4K monitors on one cable, which is why one-cable docks use it. HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort carry video but cannot charge a laptop or carry USB data, and a USB Type-A port carries data but has no native video output and too little power to charge a laptop.

question: A startup with no data center of its own rents virtual servers by the hour from a provider whose hardware is shared by many unrelated customers. Which deployment model is this?
explanation: A public cloud is run by a provider that sells the same pooled hardware to any customer, who rents capacity as needed and owns no data center. A private cloud serves a single organization, a community cloud is shared by organizations with common needs, and a hybrid cloud links a public cloud to the customer's own private environment.

question: Every page from a laser printer now comes out solid black, even a page that holds a single line of text. Which component has most likely failed?
explanation: The charge roller (the primary charge roller) gives the drum a uniform negative charge so that toner sticks only where the laser has written, and if it fails the whole drum attracts toner and every page prints solid black. A failed transfer roller leaves pages blank or faint, a fuser roller that is not hot enough lets toner smear, and a worn pickup roller stops paper from feeding.

question: A user edits a spreadsheet on her laptop, and within moments the updated copy appears on her phone and her office desktop through a cloud storage service. Which cloud characteristic is this?
explanation: File synchronization keeps the newest copy of a file on every device that is linked to the cloud service, so a change made on one appears on the others. Shared resources are hardware that the provider pools for many customers, dedicated resources are reserved for a single customer, and metered utilization bills each customer for the resources it uses.

question: A technician is removing a laptop keyboard whose flat ribbon cable sits in a zero insertion force (ZIF) connector on the system board. How should the cable be freed?
options: Pull the cable straight out by its tab
Lift the locking flap, then slide the cable out
Pry the connector off the board with a spudger
Squeeze the plug's latch, then pull the plug out
explanation: A ZIF connector clamps a ribbon cable under a small hinged flap, so the flap must be lifted before the cable slides out with no force, and pulling it while the flap is closed can tear it. Pulling straight out by a tab suits a low insertion force connector, prying with a spudger suits a press-fit board-to-board connector like those in phones, and squeezing a latch suits a wire-to-board plug.

question: A file must arrive complete and in order over a link that drops some packets. Which TCP behavior, missing from UDP, makes this possible?
options: It rides inside IP packets addressed to the other host
It sequences every segment and resends any not acknowledged
It sends data at once, with no session set up first
It adds port numbers that identify each application
explanation: TCP numbers every segment and resends any that the receiver does not acknowledge, so data arrives complete and in order, and UDP does neither. Both protocols carry port numbers that identify the application and both travel inside IP packets, while sending at once with no session set up first is how UDP works.

question: A packet capture shows a laptop sending a broadcast from UDP port 68 to UDP port 67. Which service is the laptop trying to reach?
explanation: DHCP uses UDP port 67 on the server and UDP port 68 on the client, and a client with no address yet finds a server by broadcasting. DNS answers name lookups on port 53, TFTP transfers files on UDP port 69, and SNMP manages network devices on UDP ports 161 and 162.

question: A house has fiber service from its ISP all the way to the building. Which device at the house converts the light signal on the fiber into an Ethernet connection for the home router?
explanation: An optical network terminal sits at the customer end of a fiber connection and converts the light signal into Ethernet for the router. The optical line terminal is the equipment at the provider end, in its central office; a cable modem termination system serves cable customers from the provider side; and a DSL modem connects a home over telephone wiring.

question: A technician finds a desktop memory module whose label gives a standard voltage of 1.2 V. Which generation of DDR memory is it?
explanation: DDR4 runs at a standard 1.2 volts, down from 1.5 volts for DDR3 (1.35 volts for low-voltage DDR3L). DDR5 lowers it again to 1.1 volts, and the older DDR2 ran at 1.8 volts. Each step down cuts power use and heat, and each generation is keyed differently so that a module cannot go into the wrong slot.

question: A cloud provider serves many customer companies from the same physical servers and keeps each company's data and applications separate from the others. Which characteristic does this describe?
explanation: Multitenancy lets one provider serve many customers, called tenants, from the same physical hardware while each tenant's data and applications stay isolated from the rest. Elasticity grows and shrinks capacity with demand, availability keeps a service running through failures, and metered utilization charges each customer for what it uses.

question: What does a company gain by building its own private cloud instead of using a public cloud?
options: Less equipment for its staff to run
explanation: A private cloud is dedicated to one organization, which gains the most control over its data, security and infrastructure but also pays for and staffs the most itself. Lower upfront hardware cost, less equipment to run and fast scaling during spikes are what a public cloud offers, because the provider owns the hardware and pools it across customers.

question: A video editor's workstation must copy large files to a server over a 10 Gbps Ethernet link, but its built-in port runs at 1 Gbps. Which expansion card should be installed?
explanation: A network interface card installed in a PCIe slot adds an Ethernet port, and a 10 Gbps card gives the workstation a faster link than its built-in 1 Gbps port. A storage controller card adds drive connections for RAID or extra disks, a video capture card takes in video from an outside source, and a video card drives the displays.

question: A technician is connecting a new monitor that runs at 2560 x 1440 and 144 Hz. The graphics card offers four outputs. Which output can drive the monitor at its full resolution and refresh rate?
explanation: DisplayPort 1.2 carries about 17 Gbps of video data, which is enough for 2560 x 1440 at 144 Hz. HDMI 1.4 has less than half that capacity, which holds 2560 x 1440 to about 75 Hz. Single-link DVI-D stops at 1920 x 1200 at 60 Hz, and VGA is an analog output that is not suited to that resolution and refresh rate.

question: Which Bluetooth version first added Bluetooth Low Energy, the mode that lets fitness bands and beacons run for months on a small battery?
explanation: Bluetooth 4.0, adopted in 2010, added Bluetooth Low Energy (also sold as Bluetooth Smart), which lets small devices run for months or years on a coin-cell battery. Bluetooth 2.0 added Enhanced Data Rate, Bluetooth 3.0 added a high-speed mode that hands large transfers to Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth 5.0 improved the range and speed of Low Energy rather than introducing it.

question: A desktop has begun freezing and restarting at random. With the case open, the technician sees several capacitors near the CPU socket with domed tops and brown residue. What should the technician do?
explanation: Capacitors with domed tops or leaked residue have failed, and because they are part of the motherboard, the standard repair is to replace the board. A new CPU cooler fixes overheating, reseating the memory fixes modules that have worked loose, and clearing the CMOS undoes bad settings, but none of these repairs a damaged board.

question: Which 802.11 standard works only in the 5 GHz band and was the first to add downlink MU-MIMO?
explanation: 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5) runs only in the 5 GHz band and was the first standard to add downlink MU-MIMO, which lets an access point send to several clients at the same time. 802.11a also uses only 5 GHz but has no MIMO at all, 802.11n brought single-user MIMO to both bands, and 802.11ax added uplink MU-MIMO and OFDMA and also works at 2.4 GHz.

question: An employee who used a personal phone for work is leaving the company. IT must remove the corporate email, apps and data from the phone without touching the employee's own photos and apps. Which MDM action should be used?
explanation: A selective wipe (called an enterprise wipe or a retire by some MDM vendors) removes only the corporate accounts, apps and data that the MDM delivered and leaves personal content in place, which suits a personally owned phone. A full wipe would erase the employee's own data as well, while remote lock and locate device help with a lost phone but remove nothing.

question: A company wants to separate its departments logically on its existing managed switches without buying more hardware. What should the technician do?
options: Give each department its own DHCP scope
Put each department in its own VLAN
Set a QoS priority for each department
Turn on port security for each department
explanation: A VLAN divides one physical switch into separate logical networks, each its own broadcast domain, so departments can be isolated on existing hardware. A DHCP scope only sets which addresses are handed out, port security limits which devices may use a port, and QoS decides whose traffic goes first on a busy link, so none of them separates one group of users from another.

question: An older laptop's firmware runs its SATA controller in IDE mode. Before a clean Windows installation on a new SATA SSD, the technician switches the controller to AHCI. What does AHCI provide that IDE mode does not?
options: Striping data across two drives for speed
Full use of disk space beyond the first 2 TB
Booting in UEFI mode and using Secure Boot
explanation: AHCI gives a SATA drive native command queuing and hot-plugging, which IDE compatibility mode lacks, so an SSD should run in AHCI mode, set before Windows is installed. Striping across two drives is what RAID mode adds, UEFI booting and Secure Boot are boot settings separate from the controller mode, and using space beyond 2 TB depends on the GPT partition style.

question: An old barcode scanner's wireless adapter has a top rate of 54 Mbps and cannot detect any 2.4 GHz network. Which standard does the adapter use?
explanation: 802.11a works only in the 5 GHz band at up to 54 Mbps, so an adapter built to it cannot see 2.4 GHz networks at all. 802.11g reaches the same 54 Mbps but in the 2.4 GHz band, 802.11b uses 2.4 GHz at up to 11 Mbps, and 802.11ac also stays in the 5 GHz band but runs far faster than 54 Mbps.

question: A laser printer scatters tiny black specks at random over every page, including areas that should be blank. What is the most likely cause?
options: Loose toner in the paper path
A fuser that is running too cool
A scratch on the photosensitive drum
explanation: Random specks over the whole page come from loose toner inside the printer, often from a leaking cartridge, which the rollers carry onto each sheet, and the fix is to clean the paper path with a toner vacuum. A fuser that is too cool leaves toner that smears, a scratch on the drum prints a line in the same place on every page, and worn pickup rollers cause feed failures rather than marks.

question: A desktop shows no link light on its network port. To learn whether the network card itself has failed, the technician wants to test it with no cable or switch attached. Which tool should be used?
explanation: A loopback plug connects a port's transmit pins to its receive pins, so the network card can send test signals to itself and show that it works with no cable or switch attached. A cable tester checks a cable run rather than the card, a toner probe traces which cable is which, and a network tap copies traffic on a working link.

question: A cable company installer is running new coaxial cable from the street to a home for television and internet service. Which cable type is the standard choice for this run?
explanation: RG-6 is the standard coaxial cable for cable television, satellite and cable internet: it is a 75-ohm cable with a thicker center conductor and better shielding than RG-59, so it loses less signal at high frequencies. RG-59 is a thinner 75-ohm cable suited to short, low-frequency runs such as analog CCTV. RG-58 and RG-8 are 50-ohm cables that were used for thin and thick Ethernet and for radio equipment.

question: A company must push apps, VPN settings and security policies to every employee's phone from one console and enforce them remotely. Which technology provides this?
explanation: Mobile device management (MDM) enrolls each phone so that administrators can push apps, Wi-Fi and VPN profiles and security policies to it and enforce them from one console. Group Policy does this for domain-joined Windows computers but not for phones, mobile threat defense detects malware and risky networks on a phone without pushing settings, and network access control checks a device as it joins the network.

question: A small business wants one device at its internet edge that combines a firewall, intrusion prevention, antivirus scanning and web filtering. Which device meets this need?
explanation: A unified threat management (UTM) appliance combines a firewall, intrusion prevention, malware scanning, web filtering and often a VPN in one box, which suits a small business with few security staff. A load balancer spreads requests across several servers, a spam gateway filters incoming email, and a proxy server forwards and filters web requests but does not act as the network firewall.

question: An audit finds that a managed switch still accepts Telnet connections. Why does the auditor rate this a high-risk finding?
options: It lets files be copied to the switch with no sign-in
It sends commands and the password as plain text
It serves the management web page without encryption
It lets settings be read with a default community string
explanation: Telnet sends everything, including the sign-in name and password, as plain text that anyone capturing the traffic can read, which is why SSH has replaced it for managing devices. A management web page without encryption is a weakness of HTTP, copying files with no sign-in describes TFTP, and a default community string is a weakness of SNMP versions 1 and 2c.

question: A new employee wants to use a personal Android phone for work, and the employer manages phones with Microsoft Intune. What should the employee do to enroll the phone?
options: Factory reset it and scan a QR code
Install Company Portal and sign in
Add the work email account in Settings
Install Authenticator and approve the sign-in
explanation: On Microsoft Intune, a personally owned Android phone is enrolled by installing the Company Portal app from Google Play and signing in with the work account, which creates a separate work profile for corporate apps and data. A factory reset with a QR code is the enrollment route for company-owned phones and would erase the employee's data, adding the account in Settings sets up mail without enrolling the phone, and Authenticator handles sign-in approvals rather than enrollment.

question: On a print server, documents from every user of one shared printer have waited for an hour behind a single document that stopped printing partway through. The printer shows Ready with no errors. What should the technician do first?
options: Reinstall the driver on the server
Clear a paper jam in the printer
explanation: A print queue sends jobs in the order they arrive, so one job that stalls at the head of the queue holds up every job behind it until it is canceled, and if it will not cancel, restarting the Print Spooler service clears it. A paper jam or an empty toner cartridge would show as an error on the printer, and reinstalling the driver is a step for garbled or failed output, not for one stuck job.

question: A team runs its online store on a PaaS offering. A security review finds a SQL injection flaw in the store's checkout page. Who must fix the flaw, and where?
options: The provider, by patching the runtime
The team, in its application code
The provider, through its web firewall
The team, by patching the server OS
explanation: Under platform as a service the provider maintains the servers, operating system and runtime, but the customer owns its application code, so a coding flaw such as SQL injection is the team's to fix. The provider's runtime patches do not change the team's code, a web application firewall can block attacks without removing the flaw, and the team has no access to the underlying server to patch it.

question: A laser printer pauses one user's report with a message asking for A4 paper, although its only tray holds Letter paper and it prints other users' jobs normally. What is the most likely cause?
options: The job's paper size is set to A4
The tray's paper size is set to A4
The tray's paper type is set to cardstock
The job's paper type is set to cardstock
explanation: A printer pauses for paper when a job asks for a size that no tray is set to hold, so a prompt for A4 while the tray holds Letter means the report itself, through its page setup or the print dialog, asks for A4. A tray set to A4 or to cardstock would hold up other users' jobs instead, and a job set to cardstock would make the printer ask for cardstock, not for A4.

question: A technician is moving a laptop from its hard drive to a new SSD. The user wants the SSD to start Windows with every program, setting and file in place, with no reinstall. Which method should the technician use?
options: Move settings with the User State Migration Tool
Clone the HDD with disk imaging software
Restore the user's files from File History
Copy the user profile folders with robocopy
explanation: Disk cloning software copies the whole drive, including its boot partition, Windows, programs and files, so the SSD starts up exactly as the old drive did. Robocopy copies only files and folders, File History restores only personal files, and the User State Migration Tool moves user settings and files onto a Windows installation that already exists.

question: A SOHO router lets twenty computers share one public IPv4 address. When a reply arrives from the internet, what does the router use to work out which computer should receive it?
options: The sequence number in the TCP header
The VLAN tag added to the returning frame
The port number assigned to the session
The MAC address it learned for the computer
explanation: Port address translation gives each outbound session its own port number on the shared public address and records it in a translation table, so the port on each reply identifies the inside computer. MAC addresses deliver frames on the local network once that computer is known, VLAN tags mark frames on trunk links between switches, and TCP sequence numbers put the segments of one connection back in order.

question: A streamer wants a desktop computer to take in the HDMI signal from a game console so that the gameplay can be recorded and broadcast live. Which expansion card should be installed?
explanation: A capture card has a video input, usually HDMI, that takes a signal from an outside device such as a game console or camera and passes it to the computer for recording or streaming. The HDMI ports on a graphics card send a signal out to a display, a network interface card carries the finished stream to the internet, and a storage controller card adds drive connections.

question: A developer needs to run a program built for an ARM processor on a PC that has an x86 processor. What can run the program on that PC?
explanation: Code built for one processor architecture can run on another only through an emulator, which translates its instructions in software and usually runs much more slowly than a VM. Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisors both run guest code directly on the host's CPU, so the guest must be built for the same architecture, and a container runs on the host's own kernel and processor, so it has the same limit.

question: A conference center upgrades to 802.11ax access points to cope with hundreds of phones in one hall. What does the OFDMA feature of 802.11ax do?
options: Sends separate spatial streams to several clients at once
Splits a channel into resource units for several clients
Moves capable clients from 2.4 GHz to 5 GHz
Steers the radio signal toward each client
explanation: OFDMA divides a channel into small resource units and gives different units to different clients, so one transmission can carry data for many devices at once. Sending separate spatial streams to several clients is MU-MIMO, steering the signal toward a client is beamforming, and moving dual-band clients from 2.4 GHz to 5 GHz is band steering, a feature that many access points add.

question: A RAID 5 array of five 4 TB drives loses one drive. The failed drive is replaced, and during the rebuild a second drive fails. What happens?
options: The array runs on in degraded mode
The data on the array is lost
A hot spare restores the lost data
explanation: RAID 5 holds one drive's worth of parity, so it survives one missing member, and losing a second member before the rebuild ends destroys the array and its data. A rebuild from parity works only while one member is missing, degraded mode is how the array kept running after the first failure, and a hot spare can stand in for one failed drive but cannot recreate data from two missing members.

question: After a technician replaces the screen assembly of a touch screen laptop, the image is normal but the screen no longer responds to a finger or a stylus. Which component in the lid was probably damaged or left unplugged?
explanation: The digitizer is the layer of a touch screen that senses a finger or a stylus and reports its position, so touch input stops when it is damaged or its cable is left unplugged. The inverter powers the fluorescent backlight of an older panel, so a fault there darkens the image. A disconnected antenna in the lid weakens the wireless signal, and an unplugged webcam only removes the camera.

question: Staff move between office PCs, laptops and tablets during the week and need the same complete Windows environment, with every application and file, on each device. Which solution meets this need?
explanation: Virtual desktop infrastructure runs each user's complete desktop on central servers and shows it on any device, so applications, files and settings are the same everywhere. Synchronized cloud storage carries only files, application streaming delivers individual programs rather than a whole desktop, and roaming user profiles carry settings between domain PCs but not to tablets.

question: A technician tries to fit a DDR4 module from an older desktop into a new DDR5 motherboard, but it will not go into the slot. What is physically stopping it?
options: The number of pins on the edge
The position of the key notch
The voltage the module runs at
The length of the circuit board
explanation: DDR4 and DDR5 desktop modules both have 288 pins and the same length, but the key notch sits in a different place, so a DDR4 module cannot go into a DDR5 slot. DDR5 does run at a lower voltage (1.1 volts versus 1.2 for DDR4), which is one reason the slots are keyed apart, but the voltage itself does not block the module.

question: A hospital wants patient data on staff phones to become inaccessible whenever a phone is left unused for five minutes. Which MDM policy meets this need?
options: Remote lock sent by the help desk
A geofence around the hospital grounds
explanation: An auto-lock policy with a required passcode locks a phone after a set number of idle minutes, so that nobody can reach patient data on it without unlocking it first. A remote lock works only after someone notices and sends it, storage encryption protects data on a locked or powered-off phone but does not lock an idle one, and a geofence changes settings by location rather than by idle time.

question: A phone charges only when its cable is held at a certain angle, and the same happens with several different cables. The connector inside the phone feels loose. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A fault in the charging circuit
explanation: Charging that works only at one plug angle, with any cable, points to a damaged port whose connector has worked loose, so contact is made only in one position. A fault in the charging circuit or a worn battery would not change with the angle of the plug, and a low-output charger charges slowly but steadily.

question: A user moves a monitor from a desk where it was connected by DisplayPort and connects it to a laptop by HDMI. The monitor shows No Signal, while the laptop's own screen works normally. What should the technician do FIRST?
options: Select HDMI as the input source
explanation: A monitor shows No Signal when the input it is set to receives no video, so a monitor that was used on DisplayPort and is now cabled by HDMI should first be switched to its HDMI input. A different cable is the next check if the screen stays blank on the right input, a driver update suits a display that is detected but misbehaves, and lowering the resolution fixes an out-of-range message rather than No Signal.

question: A Kali Linux VM on a technician's laptop is compromised during a penetration-testing exercise, but the laptop's own Windows installation is unaffected. Which property of VMs explains this?
options: Consolidation of guests on a host
Isolation of guests from their host
explanation: A hypervisor isolates each guest from the host and from other guests, so code that takes over a VM does not reach the host's memory or files unless a shared folder, a network path or a hypervisor flaw opens a way. Snapshots let the technician roll the guest back afterward, portability lets a VM move to another host as a set of files, and consolidation lets many VMs share one computer, but none of these protects the host.

question: Each page from a laser printer shows the intended image and, farther down the same page, a fainter copy of it. What is the most likely cause?
options: A scratch on the surface of the drum
A drum that is not fully cleaned
Loose toner in the paper path
A toner cartridge that is nearly empty
explanation: A ghost image appears when the drum is not fully cleaned after each turn, so toner or charge left from one revolution prints again a drum's circumference farther down the page. The usual causes are a worn cleaning blade or a worn drum. A scratch on the drum prints a fixed line, loose toner scatters random specks, and a nearly empty cartridge makes print fade.

question: A buyer compares four monitors that differ only in screen size and resolution. Which monitor has the lowest pixel density, so that its individual pixels are the easiest to see?
explanation: Pixel density is the number of pixels per inch, so it falls when the same resolution is spread over a larger screen and rises when more pixels fit on the same size. The 27-inch monitor at 1920 x 1080 has about 82 pixels per inch, the lowest of the four. The 24-inch monitor at that resolution has about 92, and the two 3840 x 2160 monitors have about 163 and 184.

question: A desktop runs normally for the first few minutes of a long video export, then slows sharply. A monitoring tool shows the CPU clock dropping from 3.6 GHz to 800 MHz as it slows. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The memory runs at a low speed
A power plan caps the processor
explanation: A processor that falls far below its rated clock after several minutes of heavy load is throttling to protect itself from heat, so its cooling should be checked. A power plan that caps the processor would hold it back from the start, slow memory does not lower the CPU clock, and a nearly full disk slows file work without changing processor speed.

question: On a user's new widescreen monitor, circles look like ovals and everything appears stretched sideways. Which Windows display setting is MOST likely wrong?
explanation: A resolution whose shape does not match the panel, such as a 4:3 resolution on a 16:9 monitor, is usually stretched to fill the screen, so setting the native resolution restores correct proportions. Scaling enlarges text and icons evenly without distorting them, orientation turns the whole picture on its side, and too low a color depth shows banding in gradients.

question: While removing an old CPU cooler, a technician finds the processor stuck to the heatsink. It came out of the socket even though the socket lever was still closed. Which socket does this system use?
explanation: On a pin grid array socket such as AMD AM4, the processor carries the pins and is held only by the socket's grip on them, so thermal paste that has bonded to the cooler can pull the processor out and bend its pins. AM5, LGA 1700 and LGA 1851 are land grid array sockets, where a load plate holds the processor down on pins in the socket, so the cooler lifts away without it.

question: A firewall must let clients reach an FTP server, sign in and send commands. Which port on the server carries this control connection?
explanation: FTP clients sign in and send commands over TCP port 21, the control connection, while port 20 carries the files themselves in active mode. Port 22 is SSH, which also carries encrypted SFTP transfers, and port 23 is Telnet, which gives an unencrypted remote command line.

question: A user's office is in a basement where the phone gets no cellular signal, but the phone is connected to the building's wireless network. The user must make and receive calls on the regular mobile number there. Which feature should be turned on?
explanation: Wi-Fi calling carries the phone's normal calls over a Wi-Fi network, using the same mobile number, when cellular coverage is weak or missing, provided the carrier supports it. A mobile hotspot and Bluetooth tethering share the phone's cellular data with other devices, so they cannot help without a cellular signal, and data roaming lets the phone use a partner carrier's network when traveling.

question: An administrator configures every browser in an office to use a proxy server. What does a proxy server do?
options: Hosts the company's own website for visitors
Forwards web requests for its clients
explanation: A forward proxy server takes each client's web request and makes it to the website on the client's behalf, which lets it filter sites, cache common content and log activity. DNS turns hostnames into IP addresses, a load balancer spreads incoming requests across a group of servers, and a web server hosts a company's own website for visitors.

question: A company pays its cloud provider extra so that its virtual machines run on physical servers that no other customer's workloads can use. Which cloud characteristic is it paying for?
explanation: Dedicated resources are servers or capacity reserved for a single customer, which costs more than shared hardware but gives isolation and predictable performance. Multitenancy is the opposite arrangement, with many customers on the same hardware, metered utilization bills each customer for what it uses whatever hardware it runs on, and availability keeps a service online through failures.

question: One drive in a five-drive RAID 5 array has failed, and the array is rebuilding onto a replacement drive, which will take about 12 hours. What happens if a second drive fails before the rebuild finishes?
options: Just the two failed drives lose data
The array is lost along with its data
The array runs on in degraded mode
A hot spare takes over the rebuild
explanation: RAID 5 stores one drive's worth of parity, so it survives exactly one failed drive, and a second failure during the rebuild destroys the array and everything on it. Long rebuilds on large drives widen this window, which is why RAID 6, which keeps running after two failures, and good backups matter. Independent drives would lose only their own data, and a hot spare helps after the first failure, not the second.

question: After new ink cartridges were installed, an inkjet printer's nozzle check prints every color cleanly, but text now looks slightly doubled and lines show colored fringes. What should the technician do first?
options: Run the print head alignment utility
Run the print head cleaning cycle
explanation: When a nozzle check is clean but text looks doubled and edges show colored fringes, the print head is out of alignment, so the alignment utility is the first step. Many printers ask for an alignment after new cartridges are fitted. A cleaning cycle clears clogged nozzles, which the clean nozzle check rules out, a firmware update fixes known faults in the printer's software, and reinstalling the driver fixes garbled output.

question: A company plans to move its order system from its own servers to a public cloud service. Which new risk should it plan for?
options: Buying servers before demand has grown
Losing access when its internet link fails
Running short of capacity at busy times
Paying staff to replace failed server parts
explanation: Moving a system to a public cloud makes it depend on the company's internet connection and on the provider's uptime, so an outage of either cuts off access. Buying servers ahead of demand, running short of capacity at busy times and paying staff to replace failed parts are risks of running one's own servers, which the cloud provider takes over.

question: Which virtual hardware component has its own MAC address and appears in the guest's ipconfig /all output as an Ethernet adapter?
explanation: A virtual NIC is the network adapter that the hypervisor presents to a guest, with its own MAC address, and the hypervisor connects it to a virtual switch or to the host's physical adapter. A virtual switch port is where that NIC plugs in on the host side, a virtual storage controller presents the guest's disks, and a virtual TPM gives the guest a trusted platform module for features such as BitLocker.

question: A workstation shows an IPv4 address of 169.254.31.7 with no default gateway. What does this address tell the technician?
options: It received a reservation from DHCP
It got no reply from any DHCP server
It is using IPv6 link-local addressing
It has a static address set by hand
explanation: Windows assigns itself an APIPA address in the 169.254.0.0/16 range when no DHCP server answers its request, so the fault lies somewhere between the computer and the DHCP server. A static address or a DHCP reservation would come from the network's own range, and IPv6 link-local addresses begin with fe80, not 169.254.

question: A small office has one printer, connected by USB to one of its five Windows computers. The printer has no network port or wireless, and there is no budget for new hardware. How can the other four computers print to it?
options: Reserve an address for it on the DHCP server
Share it from the attached computer
Add it by its IP address on each computer
Pair it with each computer over Bluetooth
explanation: Windows printer sharing lets the computer that the USB printer is attached to share it over the office network, as long as that computer stays on. Adding a printer by its IP address and reserving its address in DHCP both need a printer with its own network connection, and Bluetooth pairing needs a printer with a Bluetooth radio.

question: A technician gives a lightly used test VM 12 vCPUs on a host with 16 physical cores that also runs three busy VMs. What is the most likely result?
options: The other VMs share the 4 remaining cores
The other VMs wait longer for processor time
The test VM cannot start until 12 cores are free
The test VM finishes its own tasks faster
explanation: Every vCPU has to be scheduled onto a physical core, so giving a VM far more vCPUs than its work needs adds scheduling work and makes busy VMs wait longer for processor time. Extra vCPUs do not speed up a light workload, and vCPUs are not dedicated cores, so the test VM starts normally and the other VMs can still run on all 16 cores.

question: A technician needs a VM to join the office LAN as a separate device that gets its own IP address from the network's DHCP server. Which mode should the VM's virtual adapter use?
explanation: Bridged mode connects the VM's virtual adapter straight to the physical network, so the VM appears on the LAN as its own device and leases its own address from the network's DHCP server. NAT mode hides the VM behind the host's address, host-only mode lets it reach just the host and other VMs on that virtual network, and an internal network connects VMs only to each other.

question: Over several weeks, every page from a laser printer has grown steadily lighter across the whole sheet, with no streaks, smears or marks. What should the technician check first?
options: The temperature of the fuser unit
The grip of the pickup roller
explanation: Print that fades evenly over weeks, with no streaks or smears, is the classic sign of toner running out, so the toner level is the first thing to check before replacing the cartridge. A fuser that is too cool lets toner smear or rub off, a worn pickup roller causes feed failures, and a driver problem garbles output, but none of these makes pages steadily lighter.

question: A technician tidies the patch cables in a small office's network cabinet, running them through cable managers instead of leaving them in a tangle. What is the main benefit?
options: Higher data rates on each run
Faster tracing when a link fails
Longer runs before the signal fades
explanation: Cable management keeps each patch cable traceable from port to port, which makes faults quicker to find and fix and also keeps air moving through the cabinet. A cable's data rate depends on its category, surge protection comes from a surge protector, and the distance a signal can travel is set by the cabling standard, so routing cables neatly changes none of these.

question: A new VM will not start, and Task Manager on the host shows Virtualization: Disabled, although the processor supports Intel VT-x. What should the technician do?
options: Update the processor driver in Device Manager
Install the guest tools inside the VM
explanation: Hypervisors need the processor's virtualization extensions (Intel VT-x or AMD-V), and when Task Manager reports them as disabled on a CPU that has them, they are turned off in the UEFI firmware and must be enabled there. Reinstalling the hypervisor or updating a processor driver cannot change a firmware setting, and guest tools are installed inside a VM that is already running.

question: A laptop's screen was cracked in a fall, and black, ink-like blotches now spread slowly outward from the crack. Which part of the display is damaged?
explanation: Black blotches that spread from a crack are liquid crystal leaking from broken cells in the LCD panel, and the only repair is a new panel. A cracked cover glass or digitizer leaves the picture intact even when touch fails, and a failed backlight dims the picture, usually across the whole screen, rather than leaving spreading black patches.

question: A technician is given the block 10.10.10.0/26 for a new office network. How many of its addresses can be assigned to hosts?
explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits, so the block holds 2 to the power of 6, or 64, addresses, and removing the network and broadcast addresses leaves 62 for hosts. The figure 64 forgets those two reserved addresses, while 30 and 32 are the usable and total counts of a /27, which has one host bit fewer.

question: USB4 uses only the USB-C connector and can tunnel DisplayPort and PCI Express traffic alongside USB data. Which earlier interface is the USB4 protocol based on?
explanation: USB4 is based on the Thunderbolt 3 protocol, which Intel contributed to the USB standards body, so the first version of USB4 matches its 40 Gbps over a USB-C cable. Thunderbolt 2 ran at 20 Gbps over a Mini DisplayPort connector. USB 3.1 Gen 2 and USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 are the earlier USB modes at 10 and 20 Gbps, but USB4 was not built by extending them.

question: A graphics card needs one 8-pin PCIe power connector, and its maker recommends at least a 650 W power supply. The computer has a 450 W power supply with only a 6-pin PCIe connector. What should the technician do?
options: Install a 550 W Gold PSU with an 8-pin PCIe cable
Install a 750 W Bronze PSU with an 8-pin PCIe cable
Keep the 450 W PSU with a SATA to 8-pin adapter
Keep the 450 W PSU with a 6-pin to 8-pin adapter
explanation: A replacement power supply must have the connector a graphics card needs and at least the wattage its maker recommends, whatever its 80 Plus efficiency rating. A 750 W Bronze unit with an 8-pin cable meets both needs, while a 550 W Gold unit wastes less power as heat but still falls short of 650 W, and adapters on the 450 W unit supply the plug but not the capacity and can overload the cable.

question: A technician installs a known-good NVMe SSD on a new motherboard, but the drive is missing from the firmware's list of detected storage devices. Which setting should the technician check?
explanation: On a board whose M.2 slot accepts both SATA and NVMe drives, a firmware setting (named differently by each maker) chooses the slot's mode, and an NVMe drive is not detected while the slot is set to SATA. The boot device priority only orders drives that are already detected, IPv4 PXE support lets the computer start from the network, and SATA port hot plug lets drives on the SATA ports be swapped while the computer runs.

question: A technician moves a data drive from another computer into a Windows PC, and Disk Management lists the drive as Foreign. What does this status mean?
options: A clone whose disk signature is already in use
A dynamic disk created on another computer
A volume with a Linux file system
A BitLocker volume from another computer
explanation: Windows marks a dynamic disk as Foreign when its configuration was created on a different computer, and importing the foreign disk in Disk Management makes its volumes usable. A BitLocker volume from another computer appears locked until its key is entered, a clone whose disk signature is already in use is set Offline, and a Linux file system simply cannot be read by Windows.

question: A user wants one stylus for a phone and a tablet from different makers. It must work on both touchscreens with no pairing, charging or app. Which type should the technician recommend?
options: A resistive stylus with a hard plastic tip
A passive stylus with a conductive rubber tip
An active stylus with pressure sensing
An EMR stylus with no internal battery
explanation: Nearly all phone and tablet touchscreens are capacitive, so a passive stylus with a conductive tip works on any of them, as a fingertip does, with no pairing or power. An active stylus needs a battery and a screen that supports its protocol, an EMR stylus has no battery but works only on screens built with an EMR digitizer, and a hard resistive stylus works only on older resistive screens.

question: A direct thermal receipt printer worked normally until its paper roll was replaced. Since then, it feeds out receipts that are completely blank. What is the most likely cause?
options: The driver is sending the wrong printer language
The coated side faces away from the head
The printer's ink ribbon has run out
The print head needs to be cleaned
explanation: Direct thermal paper darkens only on its heat-sensitive coated side, so a roll loaded with that side away from the print head produces blank receipts. A fingernail scratch leaves a dark mark on the coated side, which shows which side should face the print head.
