question: A projector was moved closer to the screen to make the picture smaller. The whole picture is now blurry, although the laptop's own display is sharp. Which control should the technician adjust?
explanation: A projector's focus depends on the distance between the lens and the screen, so moving it closer or farther blurs the picture until the focus ring is turned. The zoom ring changes the size of the picture, keystone correction squares up a picture that is wider at one edge, and the lamp mode trades brightness for lamp life; none of them sharpens a picture that is out of focus.

question: A workstation's network card was set by hand to 100 Mbps full duplex. Its switch port reports 100 Mbps half duplex and many late collisions, and file transfers crawl. What should the technician do?
options: Replace the patch cable with Cat 6
Enable flow control on the switch port
Move the port to a different VLAN
explanation: A network card fixed at full duplex does not negotiate, so a switch port left on auto detects the speed but falls back to half duplex, and the mismatch causes late collisions and very slow transfers. Setting both ends to auto-negotiate, or both to the same fixed values, clears it; flow control manages congestion, a new cable fixes physical faults, and a VLAN change only alters which network the port joins.

question: An Android phone has a small oval port that takes a plug either way up. The laptop has only flat rectangular ports that take a plug one way. Which cable connects the phone to the laptop?
explanation: USB-C is the small, reversible connector on current Android phones, and USB-A is the flat rectangular port that takes its plug only one way, so a USB-C to USB-A cable joins them. Micro-USB plugs fit one way only and belong to older phones, Lightning is Apple's reversible connector for iPhones before the iPhone 15, and a cable with a USB-C end for the laptop would not fit its USB-A ports.

question: A user's Bluetooth headset crackles whenever the microwave oven in the break room is running. Which frequency band do the headset and the oven share?
explanation: Bluetooth transmits in the unlicensed 2.4 GHz band, the same band that microwave ovens and 802.11b, g and n Wi-Fi use, and it hops rapidly between channels to limit interference. NFC works at 13.56 MHz, the 900 MHz band carries UHF RFID and Z-Wave in North America, and 5.8 GHz is used by some cordless phones and the upper 5 GHz Wi-Fi channels.

question: A technician needs a replacement cable for a monitor whose only video input is VGA. Which connector must the cable have?
options: A 19-pin plug with two angled corners
A 15-pin plug with its pins in three rows
A 24-pin plug with a flat blade
A 20-pin plug with one angled corner
explanation: VGA uses a 15-pin D-sub connector (DE-15) with its pins in three rows of five, and it carries analog video. HDMI uses a 19-pin plug with two angled corners, full-size DisplayPort uses a 20-pin plug with one angled corner, and dual-link DVI-D uses 24 pins beside a flat blade.

question: A user prints a 10-page report with the number of copies set to five, and the printer delivers all five copies of page 1, then all five of page 2, and so on. Which setting fixes this?
explanation: Collate prints each copy as a complete set in page order, pages 1 to 10 and then 1 to 10 again, instead of grouping every copy of each page together. Reverse order changes which page comes out first, duplex prints on both sides of the sheet, and draft lowers print quality to save ink or toner.

question: A technician installs a new NVMe SSD as a second drive in a laptop. File Explorer does not show it, and opening Disk Management brings up a prompt to choose MBR or GPT for it. What should the technician do?
options: Run chkdsk /f to repair the drive's file system
Initialize the disk and create a volume
Update the SSD firmware and restart the laptop
Assign the drive a letter in Disk Management
explanation: A disk with no partition table must be initialized by choosing MBR or GPT, and then given a volume, before File Explorer can show it. Disk Management asks for that choice when it opens and finds such a disk. A drive letter can only be given to a volume that exists, a firmware update fixes drive faults rather than a blank disk, and chkdsk repairs a file system that a new drive does not yet have.

question: While hardening a home router, a technician finds that Wi-Fi Protected Setup is enabled. Why do security guides recommend turning this feature off?
options: It lets devices open inbound ports on their own
It reveals the passphrase to anyone who guesses the PIN
It leaves wireless traffic unencrypted for anyone nearby
It makes the router's admin page reachable from the internet
explanation: The WPS PIN is checked in two halves, so an attacker needs at most 11,000 guesses to find it, and the router then hands over the Wi-Fi passphrase. An admin page reachable from the internet comes from remote management, devices opening their own ports is what UPnP allows, and unencrypted traffic comes from running the network open instead of with WPA2 or WPA3.

question: A laptop is connected to a projector by HDMI. The slides appear correctly, but the sound plays from the laptop's own speakers instead of through the projector. What should the technician change?
explanation: HDMI carries sound as well as video, but the operating system sends sound only to the output chosen as its default playback device, so the projector must be selected there. The projector's audio input setting matters only once sound is arriving over HDMI, its speaker volume cannot help while the laptop keeps the sound, and the display mode controls where the picture appears.

question: During a network boot, a computer downloads its boot file from a server over UDP, with no session and no sign-in. Which protocol carries the download?
explanation: TFTP moves files over UDP port 69 with no session and no sign-in, which keeps it simple enough to build into network boot firmware and small network devices. FTP and FTPS run over TCP and require a sign-in, with FTPS adding TLS encryption, and SFTP transfers files inside an encrypted SSH session on port 22.

question: A technician installs a graphics card in the lower full-length PCIe slot, which the motherboard manual says is wired for four lanes. What is the result?
options: It is not detected at startup
It works at the full x16 link width
It halts the computer during POST
It works at a reduced link width
explanation: A PCIe card trains its link at the widest width that both it and the slot support, so a graphics card in a full-length slot wired for four lanes works, but with a quarter of the x16 bandwidth. It would run at x16 only in a slot wired for 16 lanes, and a card that is missing at startup or halts POST points to seating, power or a fault rather than the slot's wiring.

question: A technician opens a printer's setup page at an address that begins with http:// and includes no port number. Which port does the browser connect to?
explanation: A browser uses port 80 for an http:// address that names no port, since port 80 is the default for plain HTTP. Port 443 is the default for https:// addresses, while 8080 and 8443 are common alternative ports for HTTP and HTTPS that have to be typed into the address.

question: A user's headset has separate 3.5 mm plugs for the headphones and the microphone, but the laptop has one combined headset jack. Which adapter lets both work through that jack?
options: A TRS extension cable for each plug
A 3.5 mm to 6.35 mm headphone adapter
A Y-splitter ending in a TRRS plug
A Y-splitter ending in a TRS plug
explanation: A combined headset jack takes one four-conductor TRRS plug that carries both stereo sound and the microphone, so a headset with separate headphone and microphone plugs needs a Y-splitter that ends in a TRRS plug. A splitter that ends in a three-conductor TRS plug has no microphone contact and serves to share stereo sound between two sets of headphones, a 3.5 mm to 6.35 mm adapter fits headphones to larger studio jacks, and extension cables add length without combining the plugs.

question: A print shop beside an electrical substation keeps losing its internet connection to electromagnetic interference from the substation. Which connection type would be immune to that interference?
explanation: Fiber carries data as pulses of light through glass, so electromagnetic interference cannot disturb the signal. DSL and cable broadband carry electrical signals over copper that interference can corrupt, and cellular broadband travels by radio, which is itself open to interference.

question: A company is adding smart thermostats and IP cameras that seldom receive firmware updates. Which step limits what an attacker could reach if one of these devices were compromised?
options: Place them on a separate VLAN
Power them from a PoE switch
explanation: Putting IoT devices on their own VLAN, with firewall rules that block traffic toward core systems, contains an attacker who takes over one of them. A DHCP reservation keeps a device's address stable, PoE supplies power over the network cable, and MAC filtering controls which devices may join the network but not what a device that has joined can reach.

question: A user reads mail on a phone, a tablet and a laptop and wants folders, deletions and read status to match on all three. Which protocol should each mail app use?
explanation: IMAP keeps mail and folders on the server, so every device sees the same messages, folders and read status. POP3 downloads mail to one device and is often set to remove it from the server, SMTP sends mail rather than reading it, and LDAP looks up names and addresses in a directory.

question: A server accepts messages from other organizations' servers and keeps them in folders that staff open from phones and laptops over IMAP. Which server role is this?
explanation: A mail server accepts incoming email from other domains over SMTP and stores it in mailboxes that users reach with IMAP, which keeps folders in sync across every device. A syslog server collects log messages from network devices, a database server stores structured data for applications, and a proxy server forwards web requests for its clients.

question: A laptop connects to a USB-C dock that drives its monitor by DisplayPort Alternate Mode. With a phone charger's cable, the laptop charges and the dock's keyboard works, but the monitor shows no signal until the dock's own cable is used. Which kind of cable is the phone cable most likely to be?
explanation: DisplayPort Alternate Mode carries video over a USB-C cable's high-speed wire pairs, which a USB 2.0 cable like those sold with many phones does not have, so such a cable can charge a laptop and run a keyboard but cannot drive the monitor. A USB 3.2 or Thunderbolt 4 cable has those wire pairs and would show a picture, and a cable without data wires would not run the keyboard.

question: A database server must keep running, with its data intact, when a single bit in memory flips. Which module feature does it need?
explanation: Error-correcting code (ECC) memory stores extra check bits so that the memory controller can find and fix a single-bit error on the fly, and detect, though not fix, a double-bit error. Parity can only detect a single-bit error, usually halting the system, registered buffering eases the electrical load of many modules, and thermal monitoring reports module temperature.

question: An external drive labeled USB 3.2 Gen 1 is plugged into a laptop port labeled USB 3.0. What is the fastest data rate the connection can reach?
explanation: USB 3.2 Gen 1 is the current name for the original USB 3.0 rate of 5 Gbps, so a drive and a port with those two labels connect at 5 Gbps. USB 3.2 Gen 2 runs at 10 Gbps, USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 runs at 20 Gbps over USB-C, and 480 Mbps is the USB 2.0 rate, which applies when either side or the cable supports only USB 2.0.

question: A copier's finisher still staples reports but has stopped punching holes in them, and its control panel shows a finisher warning. What should the technician check first?
options: Whether the punch waste bin is full
Whether the driver lists the punch unit
Whether the staple cartridge is empty
Whether the output tray is overfilled
explanation: A hole punch drops its paper circles into a waste bin, and when the bin is full the finisher shows a warning and, on many models, stops punching until the bin is emptied, while stapling carries on. An empty staple cartridge would stop the stapling instead, a full output tray halts all output, and a driver without the punch unit would stop asking for holes with no warning on the printer.

question: A hospital wants to tag wheelchairs and infusion pumps with small labels that have no battery and can be read by a doorway reader a few meters away. Which technology fits this need?
explanation: Passive RFID tags have no battery and are powered by the reader's radio field, and UHF RFID readers can pick them up several meters away, which suits tracking equipment through doorways. NFC is a short-range form of RFID whose battery-free tags must be within a few centimeters of the reader, while Bluetooth beacons and Zigbee devices normally carry their own power source.

question: A technician plans a desktop host that must run several VMs at the same time. Which host resource usually limits how many VMs can run at once?
explanation: Memory is usually the first limit on a desktop host, because each running VM normally keeps its assigned RAM for as long as it runs, while processor time can be shared among VMs. When memory runs out the host starts paging to disk and every VM slows down, whereas clock speed, network bandwidth and graphics memory rarely decide how many VMs can run at once.

question: After a phone's operating system update, one Bluetooth speaker that worked for months no longer connects, while the phone's other Bluetooth devices still work. What should the technician try FIRST?
options: Move the speaker away from the Wi-Fi router
Forget the speaker and pair it again
Update the speaker's firmware through its app
explanation: When a single Bluetooth device stops connecting after a phone update, forgetting it and pairing it again replaces the stored pairing keys and is the quickest fix to try first. A firmware update for the speaker is a later step if pairing again fails, resetting network settings is for faults that affect every wireless connection on the phone, and moving away from a router helps with audio dropouts caused by interference rather than a failure to connect.

question: Compared with using a public cloud, which drawback does an organization accept when it builds and runs its own private cloud?
options: Its policies must suit several member groups
It must link and manage two environments
Its workloads share hosts with other customers
It bears the cost of the hardware and its upkeep
explanation: A private cloud gives one organization full control, but that organization pays for all of the hardware, its upkeep and any idle capacity, costs that a public cloud spreads across many customers. Sharing hosts with other customers is how a public cloud works, agreeing on policies with member groups is the burden of a community cloud, and linking two environments is the work of a hybrid cloud.

question: A technician creates a Hyper-V VM to test Windows 11. It boots with UEFI and Secure Boot and has a fixed 4 GB of memory, two virtual processors and a 64 GB virtual disk, yet setup says the PC does not meet the requirements. What should the technician enable?
explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0, so a Hyper-V VM needs its virtual Trusted Platform Module turned on in the VM's security settings before setup will continue. Nested virtualization lets a guest run its own hypervisor, enhanced session mode improves the console connection, and dynamic memory lets a guest's RAM grow and shrink, and setup requires none of these.

question: A user adds a personal mail account to a new phone using POP3. Since then, mail that arrives on the phone no longer shows up in the desktop mail program. What is the most likely cause?
options: The mailbox is over its size limit and refuses new messages
The phone downloads each message and removes it from the server
The desktop signs in to a different mailbox than the phone
A server rule moves new messages to a folder the desktop skips
explanation: A POP3 client downloads each message and is often set to remove it from the server afterward, so a device that checks the server later finds nothing to collect. A full mailbox would stop mail reaching the phone as well, a server rule moving mail out of the inbox would hide it from the phone too, and a desktop set up for a different mailbox would never have shown this mail.

question: A server needs a tamper-resistant PCIe card that generates and stores the encryption keys for its applications and performs the encryption itself, so that the keys never leave the card. Which device should the technician install?
explanation: A hardware security module is a tamper-resistant device, made as a PCIe card, a USB device or a network appliance, that generates, stores and uses encryption keys for servers and their applications. A Trusted Platform Module is built into a computer's motherboard or added to it as a small module and protects that one computer's own keys, a contactless smart card holds one user's credentials, and an encrypted USB flash drive protects the files stored on it.

question: The only DHCP server on an office network failed an hour ago, and every workstation gets its address from DHCP. The workstations already on the network still work, but a laptop connected for the first time cannot reach any server. Why do the existing workstations still work?
options: They resolve names from a DNS cache
explanation: A DHCP client keeps using its address until the lease expires, so a server outage first affects devices that hold no lease, such as a laptop joining for the first time. That laptop falls back to an APIPA address, which works only on the local link and cannot reach the servers or the internet. Reservations are stored on the DHCP server and need it to answer, and a DNS cache only remembers names already looked up, so neither keeps an address working.

question: An older laptop with a fluorescent (CCFL) backlight shows a picture that flickers and dims, and a high-pitched whine comes from the bottom of the screen bezel. An external monitor is steady. Which component is the likely cause?
explanation: The inverter turns the laptop's low-voltage DC into the high-voltage AC that a fluorescent (CCFL) backlight needs, and a failing one flickers, dims and often whines. A faulty graphics chip would disturb the external monitor as well. A damaged video cable corrupts or cuts the picture, usually as the lid moves, and a stuck lid switch turns the backlight off as if the lid were closed. LED backlights need no inverter.

question: A user reprints a 20-page report that the finisher stapled correctly last week, with the same print settings, but the copies now come out unstapled. What should the technician check first?
options: The sheet limit of the stapler
The staple cartridge in the stapler unit
The staple setting in the driver
The staple position for the paper
explanation: When a job that stapled correctly before comes out unstapled with its settings unchanged, the finisher has most likely run out of staples or jammed one in its cartridge, so the staple cartridge is the first thing to check. The staple setting and the staple position are part of the unchanged print settings, and the sheet limit cannot be the cause when the same 20 pages stapled correctly last week.

question: A technician finds the address 2001:470:8b2c:10::25 on the network adapter of a workstation. What type of IPv6 address is it?
explanation: Global unicast addresses come from the 2000::/3 range, so they begin with 2 or 3, and they are routable on the internet like public IPv4 addresses. Unique local addresses begin with fc or fd and stay inside an organization, link-local addresses begin with fe80 and work only on the local segment, and the loopback address is ::1.

question: Five independent school districts share one cloud built to meet their common student privacy rules, and they split its cost. No other organization may use it. Which deployment model is this?
explanation: A community cloud is shared by several organizations with common requirements, such as the same privacy rules, and those organizations share its cost and decide who may join. A private cloud serves only one organization, a public cloud is open to any paying customer, and a hybrid cloud joins private and public environments.

question: A laptop's USB-C port supports DisplayPort Alternate Mode. What does that mode let the port do?
options: Carry PCIe traffic to an external GPU
Send video straight to a monitor
Take in power to charge the laptop
Pass analog audio to wired headphones
explanation: DisplayPort Alternate Mode lets a USB-C port output native DisplayPort video, so a monitor can connect with a USB-C cable or a simple USB-C to DisplayPort cable. Charging comes from USB Power Delivery, PCIe for an external graphics card needs Thunderbolt (or USB4 with PCIe tunneling), and analog headphone audio uses the separate Audio Adapter Accessory Mode.

question: A repair guide for a laptop states that its display has no backlight to replace, because every pixel is its own light source. Which display technology does the laptop use?
explanation: An OLED display has no backlight, because each organic pixel emits its own light and switches off to show true black. A Mini-LED display is still an LCD: its thousands of small LEDs form a backlight behind the liquid crystal layer. IPS and VA are LCD panel types, so both depend on a backlight shining through the panel.

question: Which printer type puts a uniform charge on a photosensitive drum, attracts toner powder to parts of it and fuses that toner onto the page with heat?
explanation: A laser printer charges a photosensitive drum, writes the page onto it with a laser, attracts toner to that image and then fuses the toner to the paper with heat and pressure. Inkjet printers spray liquid ink through nozzles, thermal printers heat special paper or a ribbon, and impact printers strike an ink ribbon with pins.

question: A Windows 11 system drive with a GPT partition table is moved into another desktop. The drive is first in the boot order, but the desktop reports that no bootable device was found. Its firmware is set to legacy BIOS mode. What should the technician change?
options: Switch the boot mode to UEFI
Move the drive up the boot order
Set the SATA controller to IDE mode
Turn off Secure Boot in the firmware
explanation: Windows starts from a GPT disk only through UEFI, so firmware set to legacy BIOS mode finds no boot code it can use until the boot mode is switched to UEFI. The drive is already first in the boot order, IDE mode is a compatibility setting for old operating systems that lack AHCI drivers, and Secure Boot cannot be on while legacy mode is in use.

question: An FTP server runs in active mode. Which port does the server use to send file contents to the client?
explanation: Active-mode FTP carries file contents over a data connection from server port 20, while commands and replies travel over the control connection on port 21. Port 22 carries SSH, which SFTP uses for encrypted transfers, and port 23 carries Telnet, an unencrypted remote terminal protocol. In passive mode the data connection uses a high port chosen by the server instead of port 20.

question: A technician gives a workstation the address 10.0.0.1 with the subnet mask 255.0.0.0. Which description fits this address?
explanation: Addresses that begin with 10 belong to 10.0.0.0/8, a Class A block that RFC 1918 reserves for private networks, so 10.0.0.1 is a private Class A address that is not routed on the internet. Class B addresses have a first octet from 128 to 191, with the private block 172.16.0.0/12, and public addresses are the routable ones that ISPs assign.

question: A server must find and correct single-bit memory errors on its own while it runs. Which type of memory module provides this?
explanation: ECC memory stores extra check bits so that the memory controller can locate and fix a single-bit error while the system keeps running. Parity memory can detect a single-bit error but cannot correct it, registered memory buffers the command and address signals so that a board can carry more modules, and unbuffered memory is the ordinary type used in most desktops.

question: A user on a small mobile data plan runs out of data within days of setting up a new phone, and the usage screen shows that photo backup used most of it. Which change stops this while keeping the photos backed up?
options: Save photos to a memory card
explanation: Setting photo backup to upload only over Wi-Fi keeps every photo backed up while stopping the backup from using the plan's mobile data. Turning photo backup off would also save data but leave the photos without a backup, location tags affect privacy rather than data use, and a memory card adds storage space without changing how the backup uses the network.

question: A technician configures a RAID 1 array with two 4 TB drives. What is the total usable storage capacity?
explanation: RAID 1 writes the same data to both drives, so the usable space equals one drive, and two 4 TB drives give 4 TB. The full 8 TB of raw space is usable only as RAID 0, which keeps no copy, while 6 TB and 2 TB match no layout of two 4 TB drives.

question: A technician is adding DDR5 memory to a full-tower desktop motherboard. Which module type fits its slots?
explanation: Desktop DDR5 uses a full-size 288-pin DIMM, the same pin count as DDR4 but with the key notch in a different place. The 262-pin SO-DIMM is the DDR5 module for laptops and small systems, the 240-pin DIMM belongs to DDR2 and DDR3 desktops, and the 184-pin DIMM belongs to first-generation DDR desktops.

question: On a touchscreen laptop, a stylus draws normally, but every mark lands a few millimeters to one side of where the tip touches the glass. What should the technician do?
options: Calibrate the display for pen input
Fit a new tip to the stylus
explanation: A steady offset between the pen tip and the mark means the digitizer's coordinates no longer line up with the pixels beneath it, and the calibration tool in Windows Tablet PC Settings realigns them. Palm rejection stops stray marks from a resting hand, a new tip helps a stylus that skips or drags, and the display resolution changes the size of what is shown, not where a touch lands.

question: A monitor shows correct colors each time it is switched on, but after about twenty minutes the picture slowly takes on a green tint. The same happens when it is connected to a different computer. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The color temperature set on the monitor
A failing part inside the monitor
A loose or damaged video cable
explanation: A fault that appears only after a device warms up points to a failing component whose behavior changes with heat, and because this one follows the monitor to another computer, the component is inside the monitor. A color temperature setting would tint the picture from the moment it appears, a driver belongs to the computer that was swapped, and a loose or damaged cable would change the colors when it is moved, not as the monitor warms.

question: After a power surge, an office PC's fans spin, but there is no POST, no beep and no video. The power supply passes a tester, and known-good memory changes nothing. Which part is the MOST likely cause?
explanation: When the fans spin but POST never begins, and both the power supply and the memory have been ruled out, the motherboard (or the CPU it holds) is the most likely failure, especially after a surge. A power supply that passes a tester is less likely to be at fault, a boot drive is not needed until after POST, and a faulty monitor cable leaves POST and its beep intact.

question: A technician walks an office with a Wi-Fi analyzer and notes the signal strength of the company network in four rooms. Which reading marks the room that MOST needs better coverage?
explanation: Wi-Fi signal strength is reported in negative dBm, and the closer the number is to zero the stronger the signal, so -82 dBm is the weakest of the four readings. About -67 dBm is a common minimum for calls and video, while -54 dBm and -41 dBm are strong signals that need no change.

question: Several times a day, a desktop monitor goes black for about a second and then recovers. It happens most often when the user raises or lowers the monitor on its stand. What should the technician check FIRST?
explanation: Brief blackouts that follow movement of the monitor point to a loose or damaged video cable that loses contact for a moment as it shifts. A display driver fault or an overheating graphics card would follow the computer's workload rather than the monitor's position, and a sleep setting turns the screen off only after a period without input.

question: A small office moves its email, accounting and file sharing to SaaS applications. Which dependency becomes critical for every user?
options: A local server with spare capacity
A reliable connection to the internet
Staff to patch the guest systems
explanation: Software as a service runs entirely at the provider, so every user needs a working internet connection, and an outage at the office cuts off all of the applications at once. A local server matters for applications kept on premises, patching guest systems is the customer's job under infrastructure as a service, and maintaining the code is the customer's job under platform as a service.

question: A laptop's battery now lasts only 15 minutes, and the technician finds it swollen and pushing up the touchpad. What should the technician do?
options: Use AC power until a new battery arrives
Remove the battery and fit a new one
Fully discharge and recharge the battery
explanation: A swollen lithium-ion battery is damaged inside and can rupture or catch fire, so it must be taken out of use at once, replaced and recycled as hazardous waste. Waiting on AC power suits a worn battery but leaves a swollen one connected and charging, a full discharge and recharge only recalibrates the charge gauge, and a firmware update cannot repair a damaged cell.

question: A technician has prepared the wires of a Cat6 cable and needs to attach an RJ-45 plug to its end. Which tool fastens the plug onto the cable?
explanation: A crimper presses the contacts of an RJ-45 plug down through the insulation of each wire and clamps the plug onto the cable jacket. A punchdown tool seats wires in the contacts of a patch panel or keystone jack, a cable stripper removes the jacket before termination, and a loopback plug tests a port.

question: A desktop PC stores user files on both an SSD and an HDD. It has started making a grinding noise during disk activity. What should the technician do FIRST?
explanation: Only a hard drive has spinning platters and moving heads, so a grinding noise points to the HDD failing mechanically, and its data should be copied off before it stops working. An SSD has no moving parts and cannot grind, so backing it up first protects the wrong drive, and chkdsk /r reads every sector, which loads a failing HDD heavily and does nothing for an SSD that is not the cause.

question: A user cannot print anything to a network printer, and the printer's display shows no error. Which test shows whether the fault lies in the printer itself rather than in the PC or the network?
options: A test page sent from the printer's properties in Windows
A configuration page printed from the printer's control panel
The same document printed from a different application
A ping of the printer's IP address from the user's PC
explanation: A configuration page printed from the printer's own control panel uses nothing but the printer, so if it prints, the print engine works and the fault lies in the PC, the driver or the network. A Windows test page travels the whole path from the PC, so its failure does not say where the fault is, a ping shows only that the printer is reachable, and printing from another application rules out a fault in one program.

question: Two campus buildings are 2 kilometers apart. The link between their switches must carry 10 Gbps with no repeaters along the way. Which cable should be installed?
explanation: Single-mode fiber carries a laser signal through a narrow core for many kilometers, so it is the cable for a 10 Gbps link of 2 kilometers with no repeaters. Multimode fiber reaches only about 300 to 400 meters at 10 Gbps, Cat 6a twisted pair is limited to 100 meters, and RG-6 coaxial cable is used for cable television and broadband service.

question: A data center team installs VMware ESXi on a new server to host several production virtual machines. What is ESXi?
explanation: VMware ESXi is a Type 1, or bare-metal, hypervisor: it is installed directly on the server hardware with no operating system beneath it. A Type 2 hypervisor such as VirtualBox runs as an application on a desktop operating system, a container runtime such as Docker runs applications that share one host kernel, and a processor emulator imitates a different CPU in software.

question: A small office's only copies of its file server VM are hypervisor snapshots, kept in the same folder as the VM's virtual disk on the host's single drive. That drive fails. What can the office restore from those snapshots?
options: No usable copy of the VM
explanation: A snapshot records only the changes made after it was taken and depends on the original virtual disk, so snapshots kept on the same drive as that disk are lost with it and are no substitute for a backup on separate storage. With the drive gone, neither the newest nor the oldest snapshot can be opened, and no files or settings can be pulled from them.

question: A coffee shop lets customers pay by holding a phone within a few centimeters of the card reader. Which wireless technology does the phone use for this?
explanation: Near-field communication (NFC) works only within a few centimeters, which is why phones use it to pay with a tap at a card reader. Bluetooth links devices such as headsets across a room, Wi-Fi joins the phone to a local network, and LTE carries cellular data over a mobile carrier's network.

question: A technician is installing three access points in adjoining offices in the United States, all using the 2.4 GHz band. Which set of channels keeps the three from overlapping?
explanation: In North America, channels 1, 6 and 11 are the only set of three 2.4 GHz channels spaced far enough apart not to overlap, because channel centers sit 5 MHz apart while each channel is about 22 MHz wide. The other sets use channels only two or three numbers apart, such as 1 and 3 or 3 and 6, which are 10 or 15 MHz apart, so their signals overlap and interfere.

question: What role does the chipset play on a current desktop motherboard?
options: Runs the instructions of application software
Links the processor to storage and USB ports
Regulates the voltage supplied to the processor
Stores the UEFI firmware and its boot settings
explanation: The chipset is the hub that connects the processor to most of the board's input and output, such as SATA ports, USB ports and extra PCIe lanes, while the memory controller now sits inside the CPU. The processor runs application code, a flash chip holds the UEFI firmware and its settings, and the voltage regulator module supplies the processor's power.

question: Every job from one PC prints as rows of random symbols, while jobs from other PCs come out correctly on the same printer. What is the most likely cause?
options: That PC has a job stuck in its queue
That PC has a driver for another model
That PC's driver is set to grayscale
That PC's port has an old address
explanation: Garbled print, pages of random symbols, means the printer is receiving commands in a language it does not understand, and when only one PC is affected the usual cause is that PC's driver being written for a different printer model. A job stuck in the queue or a port with an old address would stop that PC printing at all, and a grayscale setting changes only the color of correct output.

question: After a technician resets a desktop's UEFI settings to their defaults, Windows no longer starts, and the firmware lists two separate drives instead of the RAID 1 volume they formed. Which setting MOST likely changed?
explanation: A RAID volume built by the motherboard's controller exists only while the SATA operation mode is set to RAID, and many boards default to AHCI, which presents the member drives one by one. Boot priority decides which device starts first but cannot split a RAID volume, turning on Secure Boot blocks unsigned boot loaders, and a cleared TPM makes BitLocker ask for its recovery key.

question: Toner rubs off onto the user's fingers as soon as each page leaves a laser printer. Which component is most likely defective?
explanation: The fuser assembly melts toner and presses it into the paper with a heated roller and a pressure roller, so toner that rubs off a fresh page shows that the fuser is not reaching its temperature or pressure. The imaging drum causes lines and ghost images, the transfer roller causes faint or blank pages, and worn pickup rollers cause paper that will not feed.

question: Which of these tasks is an example of using a virtual machine as a sandbox?
options: Hosting a web server and a file server on one computer
Opening an unknown attachment to watch what it does
Running a payroll program that needs Windows XP
Running a design program built for Windows on a Mac
explanation: A sandbox is an isolated virtual machine for running something that may be harmful, such as an unknown attachment, so that any damage stays inside a VM that can be reverted or deleted. Running a program that needs Windows XP is legacy software support, running a Windows program on a Mac is cross-platform virtualization, and putting two servers on one computer is server consolidation.

question: A printer often pulls two or three sheets at once from a tray of fresh, fanned paper of a weight it supports. Which part most likely needs replacing?
explanation: The separation pad presses against the top sheet as it feeds and holds back the sheets beneath it, so when the pad wears smooth several sheets pass through together, a multipage misfeed. The exit rollers carry finished pages out of the printer, the charge roller charges the drum, and the transfer belt carries the toner image to the paper, so none of them decides how many sheets leave the tray.

question: In a public cloud, what does multitenancy mean for a company's virtual machines?
options: They are billed by the hour of use
They share hosts with other customers
They restart on another host if one fails
They grow or shrink as demand changes
explanation: Multitenancy means the workloads of several customers run on the same physical hosts and infrastructure, with each tenant logically isolated from the others. Growing and shrinking with demand is rapid elasticity, billing by the hour is metered utilization, and restarting on another host after a failure is part of high availability.

question: A technician installs a high-end processor on a workstation motherboard that has an 8-pin power socket beside the processor socket. Which PSU cable plugs into it?
explanation: The EPS12V cable, often an 8-pin plug that splits into two 4-pin halves, carries 12 V to the processor's voltage regulator. An 8-pin PCIe plug looks similar but is keyed and wired for graphics cards, the 24-pin ATX cable supplies the motherboard's main power, and 15-pin SATA cables power drives.

question: A company is issuing smartphones to its staff and must stop users from removing the passcode or turning off encryption. What should the technician deploy?
explanation: Mobile device management pushes security policies to enrolled phones and locks them, so a user cannot remove the required passcode or turn off encryption. Encryption software protects stored data but leaves the setting in the user's hands, a per-app VPN secures the traffic of chosen apps, and fingerprint authentication only adds a quicker way to unlock the phone.

question: A flat rectangular port on a laptop is marked with a trident whose three prongs end in a circle, a triangle and a square. Which port is it?
explanation: The trident whose prongs end in a circle, a triangle and a square is the USB logo, and a flat rectangular port that carries it is USB-A (Type-A). HDMI ports are tapered at the bottom and usually labeled HDMI, an RJ45 network jack is nearly square with a slot for the cable's latch, and a VGA port is a D-shaped connector with 15 holes in three rows.

question: A gaming laptop renders about 140 frames per second, but its panel is rated at 60 Hz. A technician fits a 144 Hz panel with the same resolution. What does the higher rating mean?
options: The screen fits more pixels into each inch
The screen redraws the image more times each second
The graphics chip renders more frames each second
Each pixel changes shade in fewer milliseconds
explanation: Refresh rate, given in hertz, is the number of times per second that a screen redraws its image, so a 144 Hz panel can show up to 144 frames each second where a 60 Hz panel shows 60. The number of frames rendered is the frame rate, which depends on the graphics chip and the game. The time a pixel takes to change shade is the response time, in milliseconds, and the number of pixels per inch is the pixel density.

question: A technician adds two more DIMMs to a working desktop. Now it powers on with the fans running, but it sounds a repeating beep and shows no video. What should the technician do FIRST?
explanation: Memory that is not fully latched in its slots is the usual reason a PC stops passing POST right after modules are added, so reseating the memory, in the slots the manual lists, comes first. The monitor's input setting matters only once POST succeeds, a firmware update helps when the board does not yet support the new memory, and a new CMOS battery fixes a clock that resets.

question: This morning a user saved unwanted changes over an important spreadsheet in her OneDrive folder. How can a technician recover the original content?
options: Retrieve it from the recycle bin
Download it again from the web
explanation: OneDrive and similar sync services keep a version history for each file, so an earlier version can be restored after unwanted changes are saved over it. The recycle bin holds files that were deleted rather than changed, downloading the file again returns the same changed copy, and pausing sync only stops new changes from spreading.

question: A technician will run network cable through the space above a drop ceiling that the building uses as an air return. Which cable rating does the fire code require there?
explanation: A ceiling space that carries return air is a plenum, and cable there must be plenum-rated (CMP), with a jacket that resists fire and gives off little smoke. Riser cable is rated for vertical shafts between floors, general-purpose cable for ordinary runs outside air spaces, and direct burial cable for underground runs outdoors.

question: An insurer keeps customer records in its own building to meet data residency rules, while its web site and email run on a public provider's platform, and the two are linked. What kind of cloud deployment is this?
explanation: A hybrid cloud links on-premises or private infrastructure with a public cloud, so that regulated data can stay in-house while other services run at the provider. A public cloud alone would place the records with the provider, a private cloud alone would keep everything on dedicated infrastructure, and a community cloud is shared by organizations with common needs.

question: A projector on a conference table is tilted upward to reach the screen, and the picture is now wider at the top than at the bottom. Which feature can fix this without moving the projector?
explanation: Keystone correction squares up a picture that is wider at one edge than the other, the distortion that appears when a projector is tilted toward the screen instead of facing it squarely. The aspect ratio setting changes the picture's proportions, digital zoom changes its size, and ceiling projection mode flips the picture for a projector mounted upside down.

question: During a new internet installation, a technician mounts an ONT on the garage wall of a customer's house. What does this device do?
options: Converts signals on the provider's coax into Ethernet
Converts radio signals from a tower into Ethernet
Converts signals on the provider's fiber into Ethernet
Converts signals on a telephone line into Ethernet
explanation: An optical network terminal (ONT) is where a fiber provider's line ends at the customer's premises, and it turns the light signal on the fiber into Ethernet for the customer's router. A cable modem does the same job for coaxial service, a DSL modem for a telephone line, and a fixed wireless or cellular receiver for a radio link from a tower.

question: A laptop's 500 GB hard drive is cloned to a 1 TB SSD. Windows starts from the SSD, but its C: volume is still about 500 GB, with unallocated space right after it. How can that space be added to C:?
options: Initialize the disk as a GPT disk
Extend the volume into the free space
Convert the disk from MBR to GPT
Create a new simple volume in the free space
explanation: Extending a volume in Disk Management adds the unallocated space that sits right after it, so C: can grow to fill the rest of the SSD. A new simple volume would use the space as a separate drive letter, converting from MBR to GPT is needed only to use space beyond 2 TB, and initializing applies to a new blank disk, not one that already holds Windows.

question: A technician pulls a new cable from an office wall jack to the network closet. Which tool attaches the closet end of the cable to the patch panel?
explanation: A punchdown tool presses each conductor into the insulation displacement contacts on the back of a patch panel or keystone jack and trims the excess wire in the same stroke. An RJ45 crimp tool fits plugs onto the ends of patch cables, a cable stripper only removes the outer jacket before termination, and a tone generator helps trace which cable is which.

question: A technician recommends an SSD rather than a hard disk drive for a host whose six virtual machines will all read and write their own disk files on that one drive at the same time. Which SSD advantage matters MOST for this host?
explanation: When several virtual machines use one drive at once, their requests land at scattered places on it, and an SSD answers such random requests far faster than a hard disk drive, whose heads must seek to each one. An SSD's lead in sequential speed is much smaller than its lead in random access, and better shock tolerance and lower power consumption do not make the virtual machines respond any faster.

question: A company's customers are mostly in Australia, and its web application runs in a public cloud region in North America. Pages load slowly for those customers, though the servers are lightly loaded. What change would help MOST?
options: Add servers in its current region
Use a region closer to its users
Rent dedicated hosts in that region
explanation: Network delay grows with distance, so serving users from a cloud region near them shortens every round trip, which more server capacity cannot do. Adding servers, renting dedicated hosts or choosing larger sizes all help an overloaded application, but these servers are lightly loaded and the delay comes from the long path to Australia.

question: A laser printer with full cyan, magenta and yellow toner prints every job from one user in shades of gray, although other users' charts and photos print normally. What should the technician check first?
options: The quality level set in the print dialog
The color mode set in the print dialog
The paper type set in the print dialog
The paper source set in the print dialog
explanation: When one user's jobs print in gray on a color printer that prints color for everyone else, the usual cause is that user's print dialog or driver preferences being set to grayscale, so the color mode is the first thing to check. Paper type affects how toner is fused, the quality level affects darkness and detail, and paper source chooses the tray; none of them removes color.

question: A technician connects a desktop laser printer to a computer with a standard USB cable. Which connector plugs into the printer?
explanation: Printers and scanners usually take the square USB Type-B connector, while the other end of the cable is a flat USB Type-A plug for the computer. Micro-B was common on older phones and portable drives, and the rare Micro-A plug was the host end of a USB On-The-Go cable.

question: A technician is building a home theater PC in a small enclosure whose motherboard tray measures 7 by 7 inches. Which motherboard form factor will fit?
explanation: Mini-ITX boards measure 6.7 by 6.7 inches (170 by 170 mm), so they fit a 7-inch tray and suit small builds such as home theater PCs. Micro-ATX is 9.6 by 9.6 inches, ATX is 12 by 9.6 inches, and E-ATX is larger still, so none of them fits.

question: A user is comparing drives for a new workstation. Which figure is closest to the top sequential read speed of a SATA III SSD?
explanation: SATA III signals at 6 Gb/s, which leaves about 600 MB/s after encoding overhead, so SATA SSDs top out near 550 MB/s however fast their flash chips are. About 3,500 MB/s is typical of an NVMe SSD on PCIe 3.0 x4, about 7,000 MB/s of an NVMe SSD on PCIe 4.0 x4, and about 250 MB/s of a fast 7,200 RPM hard drive.

question: A new LCD monitor shows one corner noticeably brighter than the rest of the panel, and it stands out most when the picture is dark. What is this condition?
explanation: Backlight bleed is light from an LCD's backlight escaping around the edge of the panel, so a corner or edge glows when the picture should be dark. A stuck pixel cluster is a small group of dots fixed on one color, burn-in leaves the outline of content shown for a long time, and a color calibration error shifts the colors of the whole picture rather than lighting one corner.

question: A two-year-old smartphone now runs for only about two hours on a full charge with light use. Its usage screen shows no app or service standing out. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A background app is keeping the processor busy
The battery has lost much of its capacity
The phone is constantly searching for a signal
The charging port is loose or damaged
explanation: Lithium-ion batteries lose capacity with every charge cycle and with heat, so a badly worn two-year-old battery can run a phone for only a fraction of its original time, and the phone's battery health reading will confirm it. A busy background app or a constant search for signal would show up on the usage screen, and a faulty charging port would stop the phone reaching a full charge rather than shorten its runtime.

question: A phone shows full Wi-Fi bars but cannot load any web page, though calls and texts work. A laptop on the same Wi-Fi cannot load pages either, and the phone loads them once Wi-Fi is turned off. Where is the fault MOST likely to be?
options: The Wi-Fi radio inside the phone
The connection upstream of the access point
The cellular data service on the phone
The radio inside the access point
explanation: When every device on one Wi-Fi network has a strong signal but no internet, while the phone works over cellular data, the fault lies upstream of the access point, in the router, the internet service or its DNS settings. Full bars show that both the phone's Wi-Fi radio and the access point's radio are working, and pages loading over cellular show that the phone's data service and browser are fine.

question: A web server answers ping, but its HTTPS site will not load from a Windows workstation. Which tool, run on the workstation, checks whether TCP port 443 on the server is open?
explanation: The PowerShell cmdlet Test-NetConnection, typed as Test-NetConnection servername -Port 443, attempts a TCP connection to that port and reports whether it succeeded, which ping cannot show because it uses ICMP rather than TCP. Resolve-DnsName only looks up names, netstat lists connections and listening ports on the local computer, and tracert maps the routers along the path.

question: A user deletes a document from the synced cloud storage folder on her laptop. What happens to the copies of that document on her phone and in the cloud service?
options: They move to the laptop's recycle bin
They stay in the cloud as a backup
They are removed from both places
explanation: File synchronization copies every change to all linked locations, deletions included, so removing a file on one device removes it from the cloud and the other devices as well. That is why sync is not a backup, although the cloud copy usually waits in the service's recycle bin for a time. The laptop's own copy goes to its local recycle bin, and a sync conflict arises when one file is changed in two places before syncing, not when it is deleted.

question: A motherboard has four memory slots and supports at most 64 GB in total. The owner wants the maximum supported memory with every slot filled by matching modules. Which purchase meets this?
explanation: A board's maximum memory is the most it can address, so four 16 GB modules fill all four slots and reach exactly the 64 GB limit. Two 32 GB modules also total 64 GB but leave two slots empty, four 32 GB modules would total 128 GB, twice what the board supports, and three 16 GB modules reach only 48 GB and leave a slot empty.

question: A user calls to say they have just spilled coffee on their smartphone, which is still on. What should the technician tell the user to do FIRST?
options: Back up its data while the phone still works
Turn the phone off and keep it off the charger
Run the diagnostics app to check for damage
Take off the case and remove the SIM tray
explanation: A wet phone should be switched off at once and kept off the charger, because current flowing through liquid causes short circuits and corrosion. Backing up data or running diagnostics keeps the phone powered while it is wet, and taking off the case and SIM tray helps it dry but comes after the power is off.

question: A user must send a signed paper form from the office MFP to a supplier whose office has no internet access, only an analog telephone line. Which MFP function should the user choose?
explanation: Fax sends a scanned page over an analog telephone line to a fax machine at the other end, so it needs no internet connection. An email, an SMB share and a cloud folder all deliver the file over a data network, which the supplier does not have.

question: A phone held within a few centimeters of a sticker on a bus stop sign opens the transit company's timetable page. In which NFC mode is the phone working?
explanation: In reader/writer mode, often called reader mode, the phone powers a passive NFC tag with its radio field and reads the data stored on it, such as a web address on a poster or sign. Card emulation makes the phone act as a contactless card for payments, peer-to-peer mode exchanges data between two active devices, and wireless charging mode sends small amounts of power to accessories such as wearables.

question: A network printer must keep the same IP address, and the office wants every address handed out by its DHCP server. What should the technician configure?
options: An exclusion for that address in the DHCP scope
A reservation for the printer's MAC address
A longer lease time across the scope
A static address typed into the printer itself
explanation: A DHCP reservation ties one address to a device's MAC address, so the printer always receives the same address while the DHCP server still manages it. A static address typed into the printer works but sits outside the server's control, an exclusion only keeps the address out of the pool so the printer would still need a manual setting, and a longer lease delays a change without fixing the address.

question: A file server keeps its shared folders on a RAID 5 set built from four 3 TB drives. How much of that space can hold data?
explanation: RAID 5 gives up one drive's worth of space to parity, so four 3 TB drives leave 9 TB for data. All 12 TB would be usable only as RAID 0 with no protection, 6 TB is what RAID 10 or RAID 6 would leave on four drives, and 3 TB is one drive's worth, as a four-way RAID 1 mirror would give.

question: A law office's Wi-Fi uses WPA2-Personal, and the office has no RADIUS server. An audit asks for the newest security standard that still signs users in with a shared passphrase. Which setting should be selected?
explanation: WPA3-Personal is the passphrase-based successor to WPA2-Personal, and its SAE handshake resists the offline guessing attacks that work against a captured WPA2 handshake. Both Enterprise modes sign users in through 802.1X and a RADIUS server, which the office does not have, and WPA2-Personal with AES is the strongest form of the older standard, not the newest one.

question: A desktop starts Windows from a SATA SSD and keeps its data on an NVMe SSD. After a Windows update, the NVMe drive is missing from File Explorer and Disk Management, but the UEFI setup screen still shows its model and capacity. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A failed controller on the drive
A disk set offline in Windows
explanation: A drive that the firmware still identifies but that Windows cannot see at all points to a missing or faulty storage driver, which an update can break or replace. Windows still starts because the SATA drive uses a different driver. A disk set offline or a volume without a drive letter still appears in Disk Management, and a failed controller would usually keep the firmware from reading the drive's model and capacity.

question: An office still depends on a tax program that runs on Windows 7 but will not install on Windows 11, which its new PCs use. A technician runs the program in a Windows 7 virtual machine on each PC. What is this use of virtualization called?
explanation: Running an old program in a virtual machine that has the older operating system it needs is the legacy software/OS use of virtualization, and it keeps the program working after the hardware is replaced. Cross-platform virtualization runs an OS made for a different platform, application streaming delivers a program from a server without a local install, and a sandbox isolates software that may be harmful.

question: A branch office's new satellite internet service tests at its full 100 Mbps, yet web pages and remote desktop sessions are slow to respond. Ping shows a steady 620 ms to every site, with no lost replies. What problem does this show?
explanation: Latency is the time a packet takes to make its trip, and a geostationary satellite link adds roughly 600 ms of round-trip delay, so interactive sessions lag even when bandwidth is high. Jitter would show ping times that vary, packet loss would show missing replies, and low bandwidth would show in the speed test.

question: A user's laptop loses its Wi-Fi connection after 10 to 15 minutes without use and must reconnect, while other laptops on the same network stay connected. What should the technician check?
options: The DHCP lease time for the wireless scope
The channel width on the access point
explanation: Windows can switch off an idle wireless adapter to save power, which drops the connection after a period without use. Clearing the option "Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power" in Device Manager keeps it connected. Roaming aggressiveness affects how readily the adapter changes access points, and the lease time and channel width are network settings that would affect the other laptops too.

question: A laptop with a built-in cellular modem must share its connection with two colleagues' tablets at the same time, without cables and at the highest speed. Which feature should be turned on in the laptop?
explanation: Wi-Fi tethering, usually called a mobile hotspot, turns the laptop into a small access point that several devices can join at once at Wi-Fi speed. Bluetooth tethering also works without cables but is far slower, and USB and Ethernet tethering both need a cable to each device.

question: Which component is mounted on a DDR5 desktop memory module but not on a DDR4 module?
explanation: DDR5 moves voltage regulation onto the module itself with a power management integrated circuit (PMIC), where DDR4 takes regulated power from the motherboard. Both generations use a 288-pin edge connector with the key notch in different places, both carry a serial presence detect chip that reports the module's settings, and 1.2 V is the DDR4 supply voltage, where DDR5 runs at 1.1 V.

question: A file server's RAID 5 array has one failed drive and is running in a degraded state. What should the technician do to return the array to full redundancy?
options: Add a drive and migrate to RAID 6
Install a new drive and rebuild
Run a consistency check on the array
Restore the array from the last backup
explanation: RAID 5 rebuilds a replaced drive's contents from the data and parity on the surviving drives, so installing a new drive and starting the rebuild restores full redundancy. Restoring from backup is for an array that has lost more drives than it can tolerate, migrating to RAID 6 adds protection to a healthy array, and a consistency check verifies parity but cannot recreate a missing drive.

question: A hospital wants staff on thin clients to use full Windows desktops, and its policy requires the desktops and their data to stay on servers in the hospital's own building. Which approach fits?
explanation: VDI on premises runs the virtual desktops on the organization's own servers, so the desktops and their data stay inside its building. VDI in the cloud would place them in a provider's data center, application virtualization delivers single programs rather than full desktops, and local virtual machines would need more capable devices and keep the data on each one.

question: A store fixes small transmitters to its shelves that run for years on a coin-cell battery and trigger offers on shoppers' phones within a few meters. Which kind of devices are these?
explanation: Bluetooth Low Energy beacons broadcast a short identifier at regular intervals, and a store's app on a nearby phone uses it to show offers, with so little power that one coin cell can last for years. NFC tags work only within a few centimeters, Wi-Fi access points need mains or PoE power, and ultra-wideband anchors are usually powered fixtures used for precise indoor positioning.

question: A laptop's screen dims the moment its charger is unplugged, even with the battery fully charged, and returns to full brightness as soon as the charger is connected again. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: A power setting for battery use
An ambient light sensor reading low
A backlight that is starting to fail
explanation: Laptops commonly run the screen at a lower brightness on battery than on the charger to save energy, so a screen that dims the moment the charger is removed and recovers when it returns is following its power settings. A failing backlight would stay dim on the charger too, a battery with low capacity runs down sooner without dimming the screen, and an ambient light sensor changes the brightness with the light in the room, not with the power source.

question: A Gigabit switch connects a PC that has a Gigabit NIC and a printer that has a 100BASE-TX port. Both links auto-negotiate. At what speed does each link run?
options: Both the PC and the printer at 100 Mbps
PC at 1,000 Mbps, printer at 100 Mbps
PC at 100 Mbps, printer at 10 Mbps
Both the PC and the printer at 1,000 Mbps
explanation: Each switch port auto-negotiates on its own and settles on the fastest speed that both ends of that link support. The PC therefore links at 1,000 Mbps and the printer at 100 Mbps, with the switch buffering frames between them. A switch does not slow its ports to match the slowest device, cannot push the printer beyond what its port supports, and steps a link down only when one end of that link cannot run faster.

question: A technician applies liquid metal thermal compound to a processor, and a drop runs off the processor's lid onto the tiny parts around it. What is the main risk if it is not cleaned off?
options: Static damage to the processor's contacts
A short circuit between nearby contacts
Overheating from air gaps under the cooler
Hardening that bonds the cooler to the lid
explanation: Liquid metal compound conducts electricity, so a stray drop on the tiny parts around the processor can short them and must be removed before power is applied. Air gaps cause overheating when there is too little compound, static damage comes from handling parts without grounding, and thermal adhesive, not liquid metal, is what bonds a cooler in place.

question: A user wants to send a large video file from a phone to a laptop beside it, with no router, cable or mobile data. Which technology gives the fastest transfer?
explanation: Wi-Fi Direct links two devices over Wi-Fi with no router or access point, so a large file moves at Wi-Fi speeds of hundreds of megabits per second. Bluetooth tops out at a few megabits per second and suits audio and small files, NFC works only over a few centimeters at a fraction of that speed, and infrared now mostly serves remote controls.

question: A new virtual machine will not start, and the hypervisor reports that the host does not support hardware virtualization. The processor is a recent Intel model. What should the technician do?
options: Enable Hyper-Threading in the UEFI setup
Enable Secure Boot in the UEFI setup
Enable VT-x in the UEFI setup
Enable the TPM in the UEFI setup
explanation: Intel VT-x and AMD-V are the processor's hardware virtualization extensions, and when they are turned off in the UEFI setup a hypervisor reports that hardware virtualization is not supported. Secure Boot protects the boot process, the TPM stores keys for features such as BitLocker, and Hyper-Threading lets each core run two threads; none of them is needed on the host to start a VM.

question: A developer installs each new build of her app in a test virtual machine. After each test she wants that same VM back exactly as it was before the install. Which hypervisor feature does this?
explanation: A snapshot records a virtual machine's state at one moment so that the same VM can be reverted to it later, which makes it ideal for testing builds on a clean system. A clone is an independent copy of a VM, a template is a master image for creating new VMs, and suspending saves the running state so that work can continue later.

question: While replacing a laptop screen, a technician sees two thin round cables that run from the hinge along the edges of the panel to small flat pads near the top corners of the lid. What are these cables?
options: Data leads for the webcam module
Antenna leads for the wireless card
Signal leads for the display panel
Power leads for the LED backlight strips
explanation: A laptop's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth antennas usually sit near the top of the lid, where reception is best, and thin coaxial leads run around the panel to connect them to the wireless card in the base. The display signal travels over a separate flat eDP cable that plugs into the back of the panel, LED backlight power is usually carried in that same cable, and the webcam lead ends at the camera module in the center of the top bezel.

question: After a phishing attack exposed several employees' passwords, a company wants to make sure that a password alone can no longer open corporate email on phones. Which requirement should be added?
explanation: Two-factor authentication requires a second proof, such as a code or an approval in an authenticator app, on top of the password, so a stolen password alone cannot complete a sign-in. Password complexity requirements make passwords harder to guess but do not stop one that has already been stolen, full-device encryption protects the data stored on a lost phone, and single sign-on lets one sign-in open many apps.

question: A Windows laptop's built-in screen goes blank whenever an external monitor is connected by HDMI, while the monitor shows the desktop correctly. The built-in screen works again as soon as the cable is unplugged. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: The display cable inside the lid has worked loose
The display mode is set to second screen only
The backlight of the built-in screen has failed
The lid sensor is stuck in the closed position
explanation: Windows can show the picture on the laptop screen only, on both screens, or on the second screen only, and that last mode blanks the built-in screen just while an external display is attached. A failed backlight or a loose display cable would leave the built-in screen dark with the monitor unplugged too, and a lid sensor stuck closed would keep treating the lid as shut after the monitor was removed.

question: A DHCP scope serves 192.168.1.0/24, and an exclusion range covers 192.168.1.1 to 192.168.1.20. Which problem is this exclusion meant to prevent?
options: Clients receiving an incorrect default gateway
Leases handed out by a rogue DHCP server
Exhaustion of the pool by guest devices
explanation: An exclusion range stops the DHCP server from leasing addresses that are already set by hand on devices such as the router, servers and printers, so no client is given an address that another device is using. The gateway that clients receive comes from a scope option, a rogue server is blocked by DHCP snooping on the switch, and excluding addresses makes the pool smaller rather than protecting it from exhaustion.

question: A user asks a technician to add memory to a compact desktop computer whose memory chips are all soldered to the system board. What should the technician recommend?
options: Fit a SO-DIMM in the open memory slot
Buy a model with more memory built in
Replace both modules with a matched pair
Install a module through the access panel
explanation: Memory chips soldered to the system board cannot be replaced or added to, so more memory means a computer bought with a larger amount built in. Fitting a SO-DIMM in an open slot suits a laptop that has one, installing a module through an access panel suits models with socketed memory behind a cover, and replacing both modules with a matched pair is how a desktop with DIMM slots is upgraded.

question: An accounting firm has a router and several wired desktops but no Wi-Fi. Staff laptops and phones now need to join the same network as the desktops. What should the technician install?
options: A wireless card in each desktop
A range extender beside the router
An access point cabled to the router
A cellular hotspot for the office
explanation: An access point cabled to the existing network joins wireless clients to that network, so the laptops and phones share the desktops' subnet, DHCP server and file shares. A range extender can only repeat a Wi-Fi network that already exists, wireless cards in the desktops do nothing for the laptops and phones, and a cellular hotspot puts its clients on a separate network that reaches the internet through the mobile carrier.

question: A design firm wants its remote staff to reach full Windows desktops from home laptops and tablets, but it does not want to buy, house or maintain any servers for them. Which approach fits?
explanation: VDI in the cloud, often sold as desktop as a service, runs the virtual desktops in a provider's data center, so the company needs no servers of its own. VDI on premises would require the firm to buy and run its own servers, application virtualization delivers single programs rather than full desktops, and local virtual machines cannot run on tablets.

question: Which PSU connector, with four pins in a row, was the standard power plug for IDE hard drives and optical drives?
explanation: The 4-pin Molex connector carries +12 V and +5 V and powered IDE hard drives and optical drives for many years. The smaller 4-pin Berg connector powered floppy drives, the flat 15-pin SATA connector powers SATA drives, and 6-pin and 8-pin PCIe connectors feed graphics cards.

question: A technician replaces a laptop's M.2 wireless card. Afterward, the laptop lists only the strongest nearby networks and loses its connection a few meters from the access point. What is the most likely cause?
options: Airplane mode is turned on in Windows
The antenna leads are not connected
The driver for the card is not installed
The wireless radio is disabled in UEFI
explanation: A wireless card whose antenna leads are left unplugged can still pick up strong signals at close range, so it finds only the nearest networks and drops them as the laptop moves away. A missing driver, airplane mode or a radio disabled in the UEFI settings would each leave the laptop with no wireless networks at all, not a weak connection.

question: A company puts its IP phones in one VLAN and its computers in another, each VLAN with its own subnet. A softphone on a computer must reach the call server in the phone VLAN. Which device can pass traffic between the two VLANs?
explanation: Each VLAN is a separate broadcast domain with its own subnet, so traffic between VLANs must be routed by a router or a Layer 3 switch. A bridge forwards frames by MAC address within one network and cannot move traffic between subnets, a repeater only regenerates the signal, and a PoE injector only supplies power to a device over its Ethernet cable.

question: An administrator must divide 192.168.50.0/24 into four equal subnets that together use the whole range. Which subnet mask should each subnet use?
explanation: Four subnets need 2 borrowed bits, since 2 to the power of 2 is 4, so the prefix grows from /24 to /26, the mask 255.255.255.192, and each subnet has 64 addresses. The mask 255.255.255.128 (/25) makes only two subnets, 255.255.255.224 (/27) makes eight, and 255.255.255.240 (/28) makes sixteen, so none of them splits the range into four.

question: A user replaces an iPhone 12 with an iPhone 16 and finds that the old charging cable will not plug into the new phone. Which connector is on the phone end of the old cable?
explanation: Every iPhone from the iPhone 5 through the iPhone 14 uses Lightning, an eight-pin reversible connector that is Apple's own design rather than an industry standard. The iPhone 15 and later use USB-C, so a USB-C cable would fit the new phone. The 30-pin dock connector was Apple's port before the iPhone 5, and USB Micro-B was the usual port on older Android phones.

question: An MDM compliance policy requires a passcode on every enrolled phone. An employee's enrolled personal phone has none, and the employee refuses to set one. What normally happens right away when the MDM marks the phone noncompliant?
options: Its corporate apps and data are removed
The entire phone is erased remotely
Its location is reported to IT staff
explanation: When an enrolled phone breaks a compliance rule such as a required passcode, its access to corporate email and other company resources is normally blocked at once, until the rule is met. Some policies also remove the corporate apps and data if the phone stays noncompliant past a grace period, the same selective wipe used when an employee leaves. Erasing the entire phone suits a stolen company-owned device, and reporting the location helps recover a lost phone.

question: A technician wants to reuse an older PSU, but its main motherboard cable has four fewer pins than the socket on the new motherboard. Which adapter makes up the difference?
explanation: A 20-pin to 24-pin adapter lets an older PSU's 20-pin main cable fill the 24-pin ATX socket on a newer motherboard. A 4-pin to 8-pin EPS adapter also adds four pins but fits the processor's power socket, a 6-pin to 8-pin PCIe adapter is for a graphics card, and a Molex to SATA adapter powers a SATA drive.

question: A user needs to charge and sync an iPhone 13 from a laptop that has only USB-A ports. Which cable does the user need?
explanation: iPhones from the iPhone 5 to the iPhone 14 use Apple's Lightning connector, so an iPhone 13 needs a Lightning to USB-A cable for a USB-A port. The iPhone 15 and later use USB-C, iPhones up to the iPhone 4S used Apple's 30-pin dock connector, and Micro-B suits older Android phones.

question: A warehouse prints shipping forms on multipart carbonless paper, and every layer of each form must carry the same text. Which printing method can do this?
options: Laser light writing on a drum
explanation: An impact printer's print head drives pins against an ink ribbon, and the force carries through to every layer of a multipart form. A laser printer, an inkjet printer's nozzles and a thermal printer's heated head all mark only the top sheet, because none of them presses hard on the paper.

question: A laptop for video editing has a 10-bit display panel where most laptops have an 8-bit panel. What does the 10-bit panel add?
options: A wider gamut than the sRGB color space
More shades of each primary color
A higher refresh rate for smooth motion
More pixels in each inch of the screen
explanation: Bit depth sets the number of shades of each primary color: an 8-bit panel has 256 per channel, about 16.7 million colors in all, and a 10-bit panel has 1,024 per channel, about 1.07 billion, so gradients look smoother and show less banding. The range of colors that can be shown is the color gamut, a separate property. Refresh rate governs motion, and the number of pixels per inch is the pixel density.

question: A technician is connecting a new Bluetooth headset to a laptop for the first time and has just turned on the laptop's Bluetooth. What is the NEXT step?
options: Select the headset in the device list
Put the headset into pairing mode
explanation: A Bluetooth headset has to be put into pairing mode before the laptop can discover it, so that step follows turning Bluetooth on. Selecting the headset in the laptop's device list comes after it is discoverable, a PIN code is entered next if the devices ask for one, and playing audio tests the finished connection.

question: A technician adds up a system's power draw: a 125 W CPU, a 250 W graphics card and 100 W for everything else. Allowing about 25 percent headroom, which is the smallest suitable PSU rating?
explanation: The parts draw 475 W, and 25 percent headroom raises that to about 594 W, so 650 W is the smallest of these ratings that covers it. A 500 W unit sits barely above the load, 550 W leaves only about 16 percent headroom, and 750 W would work but is larger than needed.

question: Editors carry multi-terabyte video projects between workstations that each have a Thunderbolt port. Which removable storage offers the most capacity and the fastest transfers?
explanation: An external SSD on a Thunderbolt port can hold several terabytes and move well over 1,000 MB/s, so it suits large video projects.
