A USB flash drive suits smaller files but holds less and writes more slowly, an SDXC memory card tops out at 2 TB and is limited by its card reader, and a dual-layer Blu-ray disc holds only 50 GB and writes slowly.

question: A technician is adding a SATA SSD to a desktop whose PSU has only 4-pin Molex plugs free. Which adapter will power the SSD?
explanation: A Molex to SATA power adapter takes power from a 4-pin Molex plug and delivers it through the 15-pin SATA power connector that the SSD needs. A SATA to Molex adapter works the other way, feeding an older Molex device from a SATA plug, while Molex to PCIe and Molex to Berg adapters feed a graphics card and a floppy drive.

question: In a company's private cloud, the finance, sales and engineering departments all draw virtual machines and storage from one common pool of servers. Which cloud characteristic is this?
explanation: Shared resources means many workloads draw on one pool of compute, storage and network capacity, which the departments of one organization share in a private cloud and many customers share in a public one. High availability keeps services running through failures, metered utilization bills each user for what it consumes, and rapid elasticity grows or shrinks capacity with demand.

question: During a product launch, a company's cloud provider adds 20 web servers on its own as traffic climbs, then removes them once traffic falls back to normal. Which cloud characteristic does this show?
explanation: Rapid elasticity lets cloud capacity grow automatically when demand rises and shrink again when it falls, so the company pays for extra servers only while it needs them. High availability keeps a service running through failures, metered utilization is the billing by use that makes shrinking worthwhile, and shared resources is the common pool that the extra servers come from.

question: A desktop restarts whenever a demanding game starts. Using a multimeter, the technician measures 10.5 V on the 12 V rail while the game is loading. What is the MOST likely cause of the restarts?
explanation: The ATX standard allows the 12 V rail to vary by only 5 percent either way (11.4 to 12.6 V), so 10.5 V under load shows a power supply that can no longer hold its voltage, and that sag is what restarts the PC. An overheating processor shuts down after heat builds rather than the moment a load starts, and a corrupted graphics driver or unstable memory timings cause crashes without pulling the rail voltage down.

question: A team must decide whether to run a small web app in virtual machines or in containers. Which statement describes a container?
options: It runs a complete guest operating system of its own
It shares the operating system kernel of its host
It displays a desktop hosted on a remote server
It runs software built for a different processor
explanation: A container packages an application with its libraries and shares the host operating system's kernel, so it is smaller and starts faster than a virtual machine. A virtual machine runs its own complete guest operating system, VDI displays a desktop that runs on a remote server, and an emulator runs software built for a different processor.

question: A laptop's service manual lists its Wi-Fi card as an M.2 2230 module, and the technician is ordering a Wi-Fi 6 card to replace it. What does 2230 describe?
options: Its width and length in millimeters
Its combined maximum data rate in Mbps
Its year and week of manufacture
explanation: M.2 size codes give a module's width and then its length in millimeters, so a 2230 card is 22 mm wide and 30 mm long, a common size for Wi-Fi cards. Four-digit chipset numbers such as 9260 name the wireless chip, a date code on a part can show the year and week it was made, and labels such as AX3000 give a rounded total of a card's maximum data rates.

question: A laptop with a SATA SSD has grown sluggish over the past year, and Windows now takes much longer to start. The drive is 98 percent full, and its health tool shows no problems. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Fragmented files that slow down reads
Too little free space for garbage collection
A SATA controller running in IDE mode
Flash memory cells worn out by years of writing
explanation: An SSD needs free blocks to write new data quickly and to run garbage collection, so a drive that is almost full slows down sharply until space is freed. Worn flash cells would show up as poor health in the drive's tool, fragmentation slows hard drives rather than SSDs, and IDE mode would have made the drive slow from the day it was installed.

question: Right after joining a coffee shop's Wi-Fi and accepting its terms page, a user gets certificate warnings on several well-known HTTPS sites. On the user's phone hotspot the same sites load without warnings. What is the MOST likely cause?
options: Outdated root certificates in the browser
An on-path attack on the network
A wrong date on the computer's clock
explanation: Certificate warnings on many trusted sites on one network only mean that something on that network is intercepting the encrypted sessions, the mark of an on-path attack such as an evil twin access point. A wrong clock, expired site certificates or an outdated root store would bring the same warnings on the phone hotspot too. The user should disconnect and enter no passwords on that network.

question: A PSU's label gives its input as 100 to 240 V at 50 or 60 Hz. Its owner is moving the computer from Canada to France and already has a power cord with a French plug. What does the label mean for the PSU?
options: It works in France but not in Canada
It needs no voltage setting in either country
It needs its input switch set to 230 V in France
It needs a step-down transformer in France
explanation: An input rating of 100 to 240 V at 50 or 60 Hz marks an auto-sensing PSU, which runs on Canada's 120 V at 60 Hz and France's 230 V at 50 Hz without any switch being set, so a power cord with the right plug is all the move needs. An input switch applies only to PSUs that have a selector, a step-down transformer is for equipment rated for 120 V alone, and a PSU rated for 200 to 240 V would work in France but not in Canada.

question: A SATA power connector carries one supply voltage that the older 4-pin Molex connector does not. Which voltage is it?
explanation: The 15-pin SATA power connector carries +3.3 V as well as +5 V and +12 V, while a 4-pin Molex plug carries only +5 V and +12 V. Both connectors share the +5 V and +12 V rails, so neither of those is the difference, and -12 V appears only on the 24-pin motherboard connector.

question: A company's cloud bill stayed high after a project ended, because the team left its test virtual machines running. Which step lowers next month's bill?
options: Add a load balancer for them
Move them to larger instance sizes
explanation: Metered utilization charges for every hour a virtual machine stays allocated, whether or not anyone uses it, so removing machines that are no longer needed stops those charges. Larger instance sizes, snapshots and a load balancer all add to the bill, though each is the right step for slow machines, recovery needs or spreading traffic.

question: A laptop's webcam shows a very dark, grainy image in every app, even in a bright room. Device Manager lists the camera with no errors, and resetting its brightness and exposure settings changes nothing. What is the most likely cause?
options: The camera driver was not installed correctly
The camera's privacy shutter is half closed
Camera access is turned off in Windows settings
The camera cable is unplugged from the board
explanation: A webcam that shows a dark, grainy picture in good light is getting too little light through its lens, and a partly closed privacy shutter is a common reason. The camera boosts the weak signal, which makes the picture grainy. An unplugged camera cable would remove the camera from Device Manager, a failed driver installation would show an error there, and turning off camera access in Windows stops apps from getting any picture rather than making it dark.

question: A desktop that worked yesterday now reports that no boot device is found. In firmware setup, the date is years in the past and every setting is back at its default, but the boot drive is listed. What is the MOST likely cause?
explanation: A coin-cell CMOS battery keeps the real-time clock running, and on most boards the firmware settings, while the computer is unplugged, so a date years in the past with every setting at its default points to a dead battery. The reset boot order or boot mode is why no boot device is found; a failing boot drive or a corrupt boot sector would not reset the clock, and a damaged firmware chip would stop the PC before setup could open.

question: A technician installs a newer-generation CPU that the board's chipset supports. The PC now powers on with its fans running but never finishes POST, and the old CPU still works in it. What should the technician do?
explanation: A newer CPU on a board whose chipset supports it can still fail to POST until the firmware is updated with code for that processor, which can be flashed with the old CPU installed or through a USB flashback feature. Thermal paste problems cause overheating once the PC is running, the CMOS battery only keeps the clock and settings, and the memory is unlikely to be at fault when the old CPU still works with it.

question: Overnight, one drive in a file server's RAID 5 array failed. When the technician arrived the next morning, the controller was already rebuilding the array onto another drive, though no one had touched the server. What made this possible?
options: A hot spare drive on standby
A cold spare on the shelf
explanation: A hot spare is an extra drive that sits powered but unused in the server until an array member fails, and the controller then rebuilds onto it with no one present. Hot-swappable bays let a technician change a drive without shutting down, a cold spare on the shelf still has to be installed by hand, and S.M.A.R.T. alerts warn of a coming failure but rebuild nothing.

question: A switch log shows port 12 changing from up to down and back again every few seconds, and the user connected to it keeps losing the network. What is this condition called?
explanation: Port flapping is a link that keeps going up and down, usually because of a damaged cable, a loose connector or a failing network card, so those are checked first. A duplex mismatch keeps the link up but makes it slow, and a broadcast storm or a switching loop floods the network and slows every user instead of dropping one port's link.

question: What is the longest passive A-to-B cable that the USB 2.0 standard allows for a Hi-Speed device, with no hub or active extender in between?
explanation: The USB 2.0 standard limits a Hi-Speed cable to 5 meters, and hubs or active extension cables are used to reach farther. About 3 meters is the usual limit for USB 3.x cables, 2 meters is the eSATA limit, and 1 meter is the limit for an internal SATA cable.

question: A technician has cleaned the old thermal paste off a laptop CPU and its heat sink. The service manual gives no instructions for applying paste. How should the new paste be applied?
options: A thin line around the CPU's edges
A small drop in the center of the CPU
A thin coat on the CPU and on the heat sink
A thick layer across the whole CPU
explanation: Thermal paste only has to fill the microscopic gaps between the CPU and the heat sink, so a small drop in the center is enough: the mounting pressure spreads it into a thin, even film. A thick layer conducts heat worse than the metal it separates and can spill onto the board, paste on both surfaces adds more than is needed and can trap air, and a line around the edges leaves an air pocket over the middle of the chip. When a service manual does specify an amount or pattern, the technician follows it instead.

question: A company backs up its fiber internet link with a 4G cellular router and is replacing that router with a 5G model. What does the 5G router offer over the 4G one?
options: Wider coverage in remote rural areas
Much higher throughput and lower latency
A path that is separate from the fiber cable
explanation: 5G offers much higher throughput and lower latency than 4G, so users notice far less change when traffic fails over to it. 4G coverage still reaches more remote rural areas, immunity to electrical interference belongs to fiber rather than to any radio link, and a path separate from the fiber is something any cellular backup gives, 4G included.

question: A user deleted several files from a desktop's NTFS hard drive and then emptied the Recycle Bin. The files are not in any backup. How can the technician BEST try to get them back?
options: Roll back the desktop to a System Restore point
Run recovery software from a USB flash drive
Run chkdsk /f to repair the hard drive
Run sfc /scannow from an elevated prompt
explanation: Deleting a file on a hard drive only marks its space as free, so recovery software can usually bring it back until new data overwrites that space, which is why it should run from another drive. Running chkdsk /f repairs file system errors, sfc /scannow replaces damaged Windows system files, and System Restore rolls back system settings and programs, but none of them restores deleted personal files.

question: A rural user subscribes to internet service delivered by a dish aimed at a geostationary satellite. What is the main disadvantage of this connection type?
options: Bandwidth shared on the local coax node
Delays of over half a second per round trip
Signal that fades far from a cell tower
A need for line of sight to a nearby tower
explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits about 35,786 km above the equator, so each request and reply travels more than 140,000 km and a round trip typically takes around 600 milliseconds, which hurts calls, video meetings and games. Bandwidth shared on a coax node is a cable limit, line of sight to a nearby tower is a fixed wireless need, and a signal that fades far from a cell tower is a cellular limit.

question: A 10GBASE-T link is built entirely from Cat 6a UTP parts: a 95-meter horizontal run and a 3-meter patch cord at each end. The link shows errors. What is wrong with it?
options: Its connectors need to be shielded
Its total length is over the limit
Its patch cords need a higher category
Its cable category is too low for 10 Gbps
explanation: The 100-meter limit for a twisted-pair channel counts every segment, so a 95-meter run plus two 3-meter patch cords makes a 101-meter channel, which is out of specification. The run alone also exceeds the 90-meter limit for the permanent link. Cat 6a, patch cords included, is rated for 10GBASE-T up to 100 meters, and unshielded Cat 6a needs no shielded connectors.

question: A family's cable internet reaches its full plan speed each morning, but wired speed tests drop sharply every evening and recover overnight. What causes the evening slowdown?
options: A monthly data cap that has been reached
Signal loss over the length of a copper phone line
Bandwidth shared with other homes on the node
Rain fade on the link to a satellite
explanation: Cable subscribers on the same node share its bandwidth, so speeds drop at busy times such as the evening and recover when demand falls. Signal loss along a phone line is a DSL limit that does not change by the hour, a reached data cap would keep speeds low until the plan resets, and rain fade affects satellite links during storms rather than on a daily schedule.

question: A host is configured with 192.168.1.50 and the subnet mask 255.255.255.0. Which network is the host on, written in CIDR notation?
explanation: The mask 255.255.255.0 is a /24, which keeps the first three octets and sets the last to zero, so 192.168.1.50 is on the network 192.168.1.0/24. The block 192.168.0.0/16 is the whole 192.168 private range, 192.168.0.0/24 is a different network that does not contain the host, and 192.168.1.0/16 is not a valid network address because a /16 network ends in 0.0.

question: A computer has a dual-channel memory controller and four memory slots, two per channel. The owner wants 16 GB of memory running in dual-channel mode. Which purchase and placement achieves this?
options: One 16 GB module in the first slot
Two 8 GB modules in different channels
Two 16 GB modules in different channels
Two 8 GB modules in the same channel
explanation: Dual-channel mode needs matching modules in both channels, so two 8 GB modules placed in different channels give 16 GB on a 128-bit path. Two modules in the same channel run in single-channel mode, a single 16 GB module can use only one channel, and two 16 GB modules in different channels run in dual-channel mode but give 32 GB rather than the 16 GB wanted.

question: Malware in one guest on a shared host exploits a flaw in the hypervisor's emulated hardware and runs its code on the host itself, from where it can reach the other guests. Which threat does this describe?
explanation: VM escape is an attack that breaks out of a guest and runs code on the host or hypervisor, which exposes every other guest on that host, so hypervisors must be patched promptly. VM sprawl is an unmanaged growth in the number of VMs, resource exhaustion is one guest starving others of processor or memory, and resource reuse leaves one guest's data in memory or storage given to another.

question: A technician replaces a laptop's SATA hard drive with an NVMe SSD. The laptop's firmware lists the new drive, but the Windows 11 installer shows no drives to install to. What should the technician do?
options: Remove and reseat the drive in its slot
Load the storage controller driver in Setup
Enable Secure Boot in the UEFI firmware settings
Convert the disk to MBR with diskpart
explanation: When the firmware lists a drive but Windows Setup shows nowhere to install, Setup is missing the driver for the storage controller (for example, Intel RST when VMD is turned on), and the Load driver option adds it. Converting to MBR fixes a disk that Setup can see but rejects in legacy BIOS mode, turning on Secure Boot answers a Windows 11 requirement message rather than a missing drive, and reseating helps when the firmware cannot see the drive.

question: A retail chain links its stores in cities across the country to its head office over circuits leased from a carrier. Which network type do these links form?
explanation: A wide area network (WAN) joins sites that are far apart, such as stores in many cities, usually over links leased from a carrier. A MAN stays within one city, a WLAN is a wireless network inside a building or campus, and a SAN connects servers to shared storage.

question: A company wants its enrolled phones to install only the apps that IT has approved in the corporate catalog, and nothing from any other source. Which MDM control does this?
explanation: An app allowlist lets enrolled phones install only the apps that IT has approved and blocks everything else, which keeps them limited to the corporate catalog. A denylist blocks the named apps but allows every app not on it, sandboxing keeps each app's data isolated from the others, and app wrapping adds management policies to a single app without controlling what else can be installed.
